title: Spatiotemporal patterns and driving factors of net carbon intensity in arid cropland systems: An explainable machine learning study in the Hexi corridor
abstract: Arid and semi-arid cropland systems play an important role in food production and terrestrial carbon cycling, but their high dependence on agricultural inputs may intensify trade-offs between productivity and carbon mitigation. This study developed a net carbon intensity (NCI) assessment framework for cropland systems in the Hexi Corridor, a typical arid region of northwestern China, and analyzed the spatiotemporal dynamics and driving factors of county-level NCI from 2001 to 2022. By integrating carbon emissions from agricultural inputs and management activities with crop carbon sequestration, we quantified cropland NCI using multi-source statistical data from 20 counties (cities and districts). Spatial analysis and an explainable machine learning framework (XGBoost–SHAP) were further applied to identify key drivers and their nonlinear effects. Results showed that cropland systems in the Hexi Corridor maintained a stable net carbon sink during the study period, while NCI exhibited an overall fluctuating upward trend (4.28–5.57 t C·ha −1 ). Spatial disparities among counties gradually decreased, accompanied by an expansion of high-NCI areas in oasis agricultural regions. Diesel input intensity (DII), cropland labor density (CLD), and the multiple cropping index (MCI) were identified as the dominant drivers of NCI. SHAP analysis revealed pronounced threshold effects and nonlinear interactions among these factors, suggesting that cropland carbon performance is governed by the coordinated effects of agricultural inputs, production systems, and environmental constraints rather than by individual drivers in isolation. These findings provide scientific support for region-specific low-carbon agricultural management and agricultural decarbonization in arid regions.

title: Using single-date airborne LiDAR features to map tree mortality timing in central european forests
abstract: Mapping tree mortality timing is essential for understanding forest disturbance dynamics and supporting management decisions under changing climatic conditions, particularly in regions affected by bark beetle outbreaks and increased wildfire risk. This study proposes a framework to estimate tree mortality timing using single-date airborne LiDAR data combined with an area-based approach. The method was applied in Bohemian Switzerland National Park (Czech Republic), where extensive Norway spruce mortality occurred between 2018 and 2021. Geometric and radiometric LiDAR features were extracted and used in three classification scenarios: (i) individual mortality years (2018–2021), (ii) grouped mortality classes (2018–2019 vs. 2020–2021), and (iii) contrasting mortality years (2018 vs. 2021). Spatial dependence was accounted for using spatial-block cross-validation, and Global Random Forest and Spatially Localized Random Forest models were compared, showing only minor differences in performance. Classification accuracy increased with the temporal contrast between classes. Scenario (i) showed limited performance (OA = 0.50), reflecting the difficulty of distinguishing adjacent years due to gradual structural and radiometric changes. Grouping mortality years (scenario ii) improved results (OA = 0.72), while the highest accuracy was achieved with scenario (iii), when contrasting temporally distant mortality years (OA = 0.81). Feature importance and ALE analysis indicated that geometric variables captured subtle structural differences, whereas radiometric features provided stronger discrimination for more distinct mortality conditions. Although precise annual dating from a single acquisition remains challenging, the proposed framework enables scalable mapping of mortality timing across large areas, supporting fire risk assessment and forest management.

title: Enhancing satellite-based turbidity monitoring in drinking water source lakes using optical classification–guided machine learning
abstract: Turbidity is a key indicator of inland water quality and a critical parameter for the management of drinking water source lakes. In optically complex lakes, pronounced spatial heterogeneity in water optical properties often limits the reliability of conventional remote sensing–based turbidity retrieval methods, constraining their application in regional water source management. This study proposes an optical classification–guided remote sensing framework integrating machine learning to improve turbidity estimation in heterogeneous drinking water source lakes. Waters are first classified into algae dominated water, transitional water, and suspended particulate matter dominated water using K-means++ clustering based on optical characteristics, enabling water type–specific model calibration. Model evaluation shows that eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), BP neural network (BP), and random forest (RF) achieve optimal performance for algae-dominated (MAPE = 13.8%), transitional water (MAPE = 19.7%), and suspended particulate matter–dominated (MAPE = 13.7%) water, respectively. Application of the framework to three large regional drinking water source lakes reveals strong spatial heterogeneity in turbidity and consistent seasonal patterns, with higher turbidity in autumn and lower levels in spring. Mean turbidity ranges from 36.1 to 62.5 NTU across the lakes, indicating substantial variability in regional source water quality. Further analysis indicates that meteorological forcing is the dominant control on turbidity variability, explaining 88%–91% of the observed changes. Overall, the proposed framework provides a robust and transferable approach for regional-scale turbidity monitoring in optically complex lakes and supports drinking water source protection and adaptive water quality management.

title: A multi-source data fusion approach for high-resolution mapping of forest structure and carbon storage
abstract: Accurate estimation of forest carbon storage is essential for implementing nature-based climate solutions and achieving carbon-neutrality goals, particularly in China, which has the world's largest afforestation efforts. Although remote sensing offers powerful tools, accurately quantifying carbon in heterogeneous forest landscapes remains challenging due to the complex vertical structure and the difficulty of scaling plot-level measurements. This study presents a multi-source data fusion framework that integrates unmanned aerial vehicle LiDAR, airborne LiDAR, Sentinel-1/2 satellite imagery, and ground inventory data to produce a high-resolution map of forest carbon storage in the Tongshan District of Xuzhou City. The key lies in stratifying forests into single- and multi-layer types using canopy entropy (CE)—a metric derived from LiDAR point clouds that quantifies structural complexity. Separate random forest models were then developed for each forest type, with input features optimized using SHAP analysis. This stratified modeling approach significantly improves prediction accuracy (RMSE%: 6.23% for single-layer and 8.61% for multi-layer forests) compared to a unified model (RMSE% = 10.23%). The resulting carbon map estimates the total forest carbon storage in Tongshan at 1.30 Tg, revealing substantial carbon sequestration potential in rehabilitated mining areas associated with ecological restoration projects. This method demonstrates that incorporating structural stratification based on CE can effectively reduce estimation errors caused by forest heterogeneity, providing robust technical support for regional high-precision carbon monitoring.

title: Detailed photovoltaic mapping and multidimensional analysis based on deep learning: a case study in Jiangsu Province, China
abstract: Solar photovoltaics (PV) constitute a key component of renewable energy, and accurately mapping their spatial distribution and assessing their environmental benefits are crucial for energy planning and sustainable development. Focusing on Jiangsu Province, China, this study employs deep learning techniques to develop a semantic segmentation network named PV-AssNet for the precise extraction of PV distributions from high-resolution remote sensing imagery. Building on this, a systematic analysis is conducted to investigate their spatial patterns, land use preferences, and carbon reduction benefits. The results show that PV-AssNet enhances PV identification performance, achieving an overall mapping accuracy of over 98% and outperforming other comparative models. The total PV area in Jiangsu Province in 2020 was 142.01 km 2 , exhibiting significant spatial heterogeneity, with high-density clusters mainly concentrated in cities of Yancheng, Suqian, and Huai'an. Water surfaces (primarily reservoirs and ponds) were the dominant land use type for PV deployment, accounting for 45.71% of the total area, followed by cropland and construction land. The carbon payback period for PV systems was approximately 2.19 years, achieving considerable net carbon emission reduction benefits over its lifecycle, with the pace of carbon benefit realization showing minimal variation across different land types. The findings provide a scientific basis for PV resource planning and territorial spatial policy formulation in Jiangsu Province, as well as a reference for coordinating regional renewable energy layout and land use optimization.

title: Ensemble-based estimation of fractional vegetation cover in arid and semi-arid regions
abstract: Fractional Vegetation Cover (FVC) is a key biophysical parameter for characterizing vegetation dynamics and ecosystem functioning, and is essential for ecological monitoring in arid and semi-arid regions. However, sparse vegetation and strong soil background effects in these regions lead to substantial variability in the applicability and stability of different inversion models, thereby limiting further improvements in FVC estimation accuracy. To address these challenges, this study applied three FVC inversion models—Random Forest (RF), Fully Constrained Least Squares (FCLS), and the Dimidiate Pixel Model (DPM)—to Sentinel-2 data, and further proposed a consistency-constrained ensemble approach. The results show that the three models exhibit pronounced discrepancies in both spatial patterns and value ranges. Specifically, RF performs better in high-coverage areas, whereas FCLS is more sensitive to soil background effects under low-coverage conditions. The proposed ensemble approach effectively integrates the strengths of individual models, improving overall accuracy by approximately 2.1% and reducing estimation uncertainty relative to individual models. These results demonstrate that the proposed approach improves FVC estimation in arid and semi-arid regions and provides a robust framework for large-scale quantitative vegetation monitoring using remote sensing.

title: Identifying algal indicators for streamflow duration assessment methods in forested headwater streams
abstract: Streamflow duration assessment methods (SDAMs) are rapid tools for reach-scale streamflow duration classification. SDAMs use single-visit indicator data as surrogates because direct measurement of long-term flow duration is resource intensive. Algae (diatoms and soft-bodied algae) are potentially strong indicators of streamflow-duration class (SDC) because of geographical ubiquity and biodiversity across moisture gradients. Algal cover and algal assemblage data (presence/absence, density, and biovolume) at species- and genus-levels were analyzed from 508 samples across 22 ephemeral, 37 intermittent, and 51 perennial reaches distributed along 31 forested headwater streams within 4 ecoregions in the contiguous United States. Random forest models using species- and genus-level datasets to predict SDCs had classification accuracy ranging from 69.5% – 88.4%, with accuracy being highest for density, intermediate for presence/absence, lowest for biovolume data. Species-level models had 0.6% – 5.9% higher accuracy for density and presence/absence datasets than genus-level models. Based on their median ranks of minimum node depth among random forest models, season (wet vs dry) was a more important factor than habitat sampled (erosional vs depositional) when distinguishing ephemeral, intermittent and perennial but habitat was more important when distinguishing ephemeral from non-ephemeral reaches. Algal cover index (categorical visual-tactile assessment) was the most important indicator of SDC. Except for the red alga, Audouinella , the identified indicator taxa were diatoms. Our findings support epilithic algal cover as an SDAM indicator for forested headwater streams. Until taxonomic tools are available for field identifications, algal cover index and abundance of soft-bodied algae and live diatoms may be candidate indicators for regional SDAMs.

title: Dominant role of CO₂ in the decoupling of structural and functional resilience indicators in the Yellow River Basin
abstract: Ecosystem resilience is essential for maintaining the structural and functional stability of terrestrial ecosystems under ongoing climate change and human disturbances. However, the long-term coupled evolutionary relationships between vegetation structural and multi-dimensional functional resilience remain poorly understood, restricting comprehensive resilience assessment of watershed ecosystems. Here, we employed first-order lag autoregressive coefficients (AR(1)) of leaf area index (LAI), water use efficiency (WUE), gross primary productivity (GPP), and evapotranspiration (ET) to quantify vegetation structural resilience and multiple key functional resilience dimensions across the Yellow River Basin during 1982–2018. We systematically explored their spatiotemporal dynamics, phase-dependent coupling patterns, and zonal differentiation across three climatic zones, and further identified dominant driving factors using interpretable machine learning (XGBoost-SHAP). The evolution of structure–function coupled resilience experienced a transition from weak coupling before 2000 to strong coupling in the 2000s, followed by a pronounced decoupling in the 2010s, with the humid and semi-humid zones exhibiting the most dramatic interdecadal shifts. Notably, the most prominent decoupling was observed between WUE resilience and LAI resilience in the plateau cold zone, while the resilience of GPP and ET maintained favorable coordination with LAI resilience. Driving mechanism analysis indicated that atmospheric CO₂ acted as the dominant factor regulating spatiotemporal variations in structural and functional resilience. In arid and humid zones, rising CO₂ increasingly inhibited LAI structural resilience while imposing weaker constraints on WUE functional resilience. Nevertheless, the plateau cold zone showed a unique response, with intensified CO₂-induced suppression on both structural and functional resilience. These findings emphasize the necessity of integrating structural and functional resilience dimensions in ecosystem assessments and highlight the importance of region-specific strategies for large-scale ecological restoration and adaptive management under global change.

title: Research on the nonlinear mechanism and multi-scale adaptive strategies of ecosystem services in the Zhengzhou metropolitan area from the perspective of water-carbon-food-ecology nexus
abstract: Uncovering the multiscale effects and nonlinear response mechanisms of ecosystem services (ESs) within the water‑carbon-food-ecology (WCFE) nexus, and developing differentiated regional governance strategies, is crucial for reconciling the conflict between conservation and development in rapidly urbanizing regions and for implementing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Addressing the limitations of existing studies—such as insufficient accuracy in identifying nonlinear thresholds at the metropolitan scale and the lack of multiscale adaptive management strategies—this study takes the Zhengzhou Metropolitan Area (ZZMA) as its research subject. Based on multi-source spatiotemporal data from 2000 to 2023, we established a research framework comprising “spatiotemporal evolution—mechanism diagnosis—zonal regulation.” First, the study reveals the spatiotemporal differentiation characteristics of Comprehensive Ecosystem Services (CES) at both the county and 1 km grid scales. Second, it introduces the XGBoost-SHAP-PDP interpretable machine learning model to analyze the nonlinear response characteristics and threshold effects of driving factors. Finally, it couples the results of mechanism analysis with Self-Organizing Maps (SOM) to construct a dual-scale adaptive zoning management framework. The results indicate: (1) During the study period, CES exhibited a spatial pattern characterized by “ecological carbon sequestration dominated by western mountainous areas and water and grain security supported by central and eastern plains,” and underwent a phased evolution of “fluctuating decline followed by localized recovery”; (2) Natural endowments and human activities jointly drove the spatial differentiation of CES, with the proportion of construction land serving as the core driving factor and its contribution continuously increasing; the contribution of factor interactions was significantly higher than that of individual factors; (3) A significant nonlinear relationship exists between CES and key driving factors, exhibiting dynamic evolution in terms of interaction modes, threshold effects, and impact intensity; (4) Based on the identification of dual-scale service clusters, ecological adaptive management units were precisely delineated, and a differentiated management strategy that balances ecological bottom lines with development was proposed by integrating Nature-based Solutions (NbS) principles. This study aims to bridge the gap between a deep understanding of the underlying mechanisms of ESs in rapidly urbanizing regions and their effective, multi-scale adaptive management, thereby providing scientific support for regional resource coordination, green transformation, and high-quality development.

title: Significant disparities in urban sustainability among provincial capital cities in mainland China toward sustainable development goal 11
abstract: A comparable assessment of urban sustainability across regions provides critical insights for achieving multiple Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), while it is often constrained by limited indicator data and the lack of comprehensive evaluation methods. This study developed a set of new evaluation indicators to evaluate urban sustainable development in 31 provincial capital cities in mainland China based on statistical data, Earth observation (EO) and geospatial data generated from deep learning and spatial analysis models in line with the urban sustainable development goal (SDG11) with indicator weighing model considering inter-indicator coupling effects. Significant disparities in sustainable development index (SDI) were revealed across economic regions and city types. Regionally, mean SDI was moderately higher in the northeastern (77.83) and eastern (77.34) regions than in the western (76.07) and central (73.14) regions. In contrast, disparities across city types were more pronounced, with Type I and II large cities achieving the highest SDI (84.60 and 82.15), followed by medium-sized cities (80.56), megacities (76.00), and super cities (72.43). Marked within-group heterogeneity was also observed in the western and central regions and across super cities, Type I large cities, and megacities, primarily associated with uneven economic development and disparities in urban living environments. To enhance the sustainability of low value cities and bridge the gap with leading cities, targeted and actionable guidance was proposed to inform policies aimed at advancing urban sustainability. These results provide a reliable scheme for tracking SDG11 progress, enabling policymakers to identify priorities and tailor interventions for urban sustainable development.

title: Coupling coordination between oasis water resilience and water ecosystem services under different water supply modes: Evidence from southern Xinjiang, Hexi corridor, and Hetao plain, China
abstract: Rapid urbanization and intensifying climate change have substantially increased the risks of water stress and ecological degradation. To elucidate the coupling mechanisms between water resilience (WR) and water ecosystem services (WES) under different water-supply modes, this study focuses on three oases in the Northwest Arid and Semi-arid Regions of China (NWAR): the Southern Xinjiang Oasis (SXO), the Hexi Corridor Oasis (HCO), and the Hetao Plain Oasis (HPO). A comprehensive analytical framework was developed by integrating the entropy weight-CRITIC weighting method, a three-dimensional (3D) vector space model, the Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST) model, the Coupling Coordination Degree (CCD) model, bivariate Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA), Extreme Gradient Boosting-SHapley Additive exPlanations (XGBoost-SHAP), and the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model. The study evaluated changes in WR, WES, and their coupling coordination from 2000 to 2020 and projected future trends. Results showed that across the NWAR, both WR and WES declined with fluctuations, while CCD decreased from 0.599 to 0.589. However, clear differences emerged among the three oases because of their distinct water-supply modes: SXO showed a “meltwater-vulnerable” maladjustment pattern, HCO exhibited “mixed-supply synergistic” recovery, and HPO experienced “engineering-regulated” moderate deterioration. Spatially, WR and WES exhibited pronounced local agglomeration and mismatch. Mechanistically, habitat quality (HQ) and carbon storage (CS) are important internal factors shaping the evolution of WES, whereas land use efficiency (LUE) contributes substantially to WR. Under the ecological protection scenario, the system followed a transition pathway characterized by “short-term maladjustment followed by long-term rebalancing.” These findings indicate that different water-supply modes reshape the WR-WES coupling relationship by altering source-water stability and ecological response pathways. Therefore, region-specific governance strategies are essential to improve the sustainability of arid oases.

title: A new vegetation type dataset in their distribution and changes across the circumpolar Arctic permafrost regions
abstract: Vegetation type serves as a crucial predictor of the Arctic land surface energy budget and its sensitivity to global warming. High-precision vegetation classification data is essential for understanding the vegetation-soil interactions, permafrost and ecosystem carbon cycle. Here, based on vegetation community structure and species composition, we offer a new dataset of vegetation type distribution in the circumpolar Arctic permafrost region from 1982 to 2020 using Google Earth Engine and machine learning. The results present an average modeling accuracy of 83%, which is greatly improved compared with the Arctic Vegetation Type Map. Our findings show that bare ground, graminoid, wetland and forest exhibit significant changes in the past four decades. The forest has the highest growth rate of 9.71 × 104 km2 per year, whereas bare land and graminoid tundra decreases at the rates of -5.21 × 104 km2 per year and -5.13 × 104 km2 per year, respectively. The improved mapping of vegetation types facilitates the quantification of the potential changes in land cover, serving as a key environmental indicator for assessing land carbon, water cycles and energy budgets.

title: Revealing the nonlinear driving mechanisms and scenario simulation pattern of landscape ecological risk in Jilin Province using XGBoost-GeoShapley and PLUS model
abstract: Deciphering the spatiotemporal dynamics of land use and landscape ecological risk (LER) is critical for advancing regional sustainable development. Focusing on Jilin Province, China, this study quantifies land use transitions and associated LER patterns from 1990 to 2020. By integrating landscape metrics, spatial statistics, and geographic explainable artificial intelligence (XGBoost-GeoShapley, eXtreme Gradient Boosting and GeoShapley), we systematically characterize the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of LER and explore the nonlinear driving mechanisms. Moreover, we integrate environmental and socioeconomic data from multiple sources with the Patch-generating Land Use Simulation (PLUS) model to forecast land use and LER trajectories across various future scenarios. The findings reveal that: (1) Between 1990 and 2020, land use in Jilin Province consisted primarily of farmland and forest land, which collectively represented more than 80% of the overall surface area; LER were mainly classified as low and medium risk, making up over 75% of the total, with high-risk zones predominantly located in the western part of the province. (2) Projections for LER in 2030 through multi-scenario simulations suggest that, within the natural development framework, the high-risk and medium-high risk areas make up 14.0%, continuing the historical rise in LER; in contrast, the ecological protection scenario reveals that high-risk areas only constitute 0.8%, the lowest among all four scenarios; under the farmland protection framework, high-risk areas represent 7.4%; while in the economic development scenario, both medium high-risk and high-risk classifications account for over 35%, which is the highest risk level across the four scenarios. (3) The effects of the driving factors are nonlinear and involve complex interactions, with the 500–1000 m elevation range serving as a key threshold interval for the region. These factors also exhibit significant spatial effects, and the driving role of a single factor varies across different geographical environments. The findings provide guidance for sustainable development and regional ecological security in Jilin Province.

title: Linking carbon sequestration function to plant community typology for designing modular units of carbon-smart urban green spaces: Evidence from Shanghai
abstract: Accurate planning of carbon-smart urban green spaces urgently requires a classification system linking plant community structure to carbon sequestration (CS) function. This study integrates multi-source remote sensing data and machine learning algorithms to identify vegetation types, tree height, diameter at breast height, leaf area index, and three-dimensional spatial structural parameters at high resolution in a typical water-network area in Shanghai. Through a five-level hierarchical classification of “characteristic zoning - dominant plant group-CS class - structural type - dominant species,” a multi-level classification framework for plant community spatial units oriented to CS optimization is constructed, generating 2639 encodable community functional units. The core findings are as follows. First, the constructed classification system effectively captures the differentiation patterns of CS efficiency, promoting the shift of community classification toward multi-level clustering that integrates CS characteristics and spatial configuration. Second, the system also reveals a decoupling phenomenon between CS efficiency (NPP, NEP) and CS storage (VegC, TotalC): the communities with high CS storage do not necessarily have high current CS efficiency, the two are independent of each other. Third, the system achieves multi-dimensional differentiation of CS influencing factors. By constructing a Carbon Sequestration-Structure Synergy Index, it subdivides climax communities into mature forest and over-mature forest, confirming that over-mature forest is the key type of functional decline, and simultaneously identifies the multi-layer coverage structure at 0.5 to 0.7 canopy density as the ideal spatial pattern that achieves an optimal balance between CS storage and efficiency. This classification system provides a directly applicable modular design menu for low-carbon planning, design, and management of green spaces in urban spaces, and establishes a more scientific classification foundation for the assessment and precise quantification of their CS enhancement.

title: Deciphering the complex drivers of vegetation change in arid regions using an interpretable machine learning framework across multiple scales
abstract: Western China's endorheic basins are climate-sensitive, yet the non-linear coupling and scale-dependent drivers of their vegetation remain unclear. We applied the MS-XGSA (Multi-Scale XGBoost-SHAP Attribution framework), integrating machine learning and trend analysis, to examine NDVI dynamics across major basins and their riparian zones. Results reveal a hierarchical pattern where climate dominates at the basin scale, while topography and human activities act as localized modulators. As the spatial scale narrows to riparian buffers, the driving forces shift significantly toward hydrological dependence and concentrated anthropogenic interference. Vegetation exhibits pronounced non-linear responses to environmental stress, characterized by critical thermal and topographic thresholds that trigger abrupt browning, defined as a sudden and significant decline in vegetation greenness (NDVI), marking a rapid transition from stable growth to ecosystem degradation. Furthermore, the synergistic coupling of rising temperatures and declining precipitation creates compound risks that destabilize the ecosystem's water balance. A distinct threshold drift occurs between scales, with riparian zones displaying higher thermal tolerance. This quantifies their role as ecological refugia, where hydrological compensation and evaporative cooling mitigate macro-climatic pressure. This study characterizes the transition from climate-controlled regional processes to hydrologically-regulated local habitats, providing a scientific basis for identifying ecological tipping points and implementing scale-specific management to enhance arid ecosystem resilience.

title: Shifts in suitable habitats and productivity of grassland plant functional groups in Xinjiang under future climate scenarios
abstract: Understanding how climate change affects the distribution and productivity of key grassland plant functional groups (PFGs) is crucial for predicting ecosystem dynamics and informing adaptive management strategies to ensure ecological security and sustainable pastoral development. Here, we combined species distribution data with environmental variables (climate, soil, and topography) to model the current and future (2050s, 2070s) potential suitable habitats for three major PFGs of legumes, graminoids, and forbs in Xinjiang under three climate scenarios (SSP126, SSP245, SSP585). We applied the MaxEnt model for habitat suitability modeling and integrated the Random Forest model to estimate forage yield within suitable areas. Our main findings are: (1) The MaxEnt model exhibited high predictive accuracy (AUC > 0.85), ensuring robust projections. (2) The dominant environmental factors influencing distribution varied among PFGs: soil type and precipitation of the coldest quarter for legumes; annual precipitation for graminoids; and precipitation of the driest month for forbs. Under current climate conditions, graminoids possessed the largest suitable habitat area (82.61 × 10 4 km 2 ), while forbs had the smallest (73.64 × 10 4 km 2 ). (3) Future climate scenarios project divergent responses. Legumes are projected to expand northeastward into the Tarim Basin, Altay region, and Turpan Basin, increasing their suitable area by 69.53%. Conversely, graminoids are projected to contract in the Tarim Basin, losing 20.03 × 10 4 km 2 of suitable habitat. Forbs show a mixed response, contracting in the Tarim Basin but expanding in the Kunlun Mountains, with their total suitable area initially decreasing before increasing, exhibiting an overall southwestward shift. Estimated forage yields generally increased with expanding suitable habitat area, with legumes showing the highest productivity. Our findings reveal distinct responses of different PFGs to future climate change. Projected alterations in temperature and precipitation patterns are likely to drive significant changes in the structure of suitable habitats and their productivity. This study provides a scientific basis for developing strategies for sustainable grassland utilization, restoration of degraded grasslands, and managing grass-livestock balance in Xinjiang.

title: Driving mechanisms of the decoupling between vegetation greenness and ecosystem resilience in the Yellow River Basin of Inner Mongolia, China (2000−2020)
abstract: The asynchronous changes in vegetation greenness and resilience (the capacity of ecosystems to absorb disturbances and maintain their functions) may threaten the long-term sustainability of ecological restoration. However, their coupling mechanisms and responses to climate change and human activities in desertification areas remain poorly understood. Here, we used the kernelized Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (kNDVI) and its temporal autocorrelation to characterize vegetation greenness and resilience from 2000 to 2020 in Yellow River Basin in Inner Mongolia, China. Random forest (RF) models were employed to quantify the dominant drivers of vegetation resilience. Results indicate a persistent greening trend across the study region, 96.62% of pixels experienced kNDVI increases. Meanwhile, resilience exhibits a pronounced turning point around 2011, transitioning from an increasing to a declining trajectory, while the proportion of resilience-declining areas increased from 18.09% in 2000–2010 to 45.85% in 2011–2020. The greenness–resilience relationship transitioned from synchronous increases to systematic decoupling, resulting in a high-greenness–low-resilience regime. The dominant drivers of vegetation resilience shifted from climate factors during 2000–2010 (contributing 51.57%) to grazing pressure during 2011–2020 (contributing 32.12%). Threshold analysis further revealed that vegetation resilience decline in the later decade resulted from the combined effects of intensified hydrological constraints and grazing pressure. Therefore, we recommend incorporating ecosystem resilience into restoration frameworks and coordinating the regulation of water availability and grazing pressure to promote the synergistic enhancement of greenness and resilience, thereby ensuring long-term ecosystem stability.

title: Estimation of canopy bulk density for modeling fire behavior in boreal forest of Northeastern China using forest inventory and multisource satellite remote sensing data
abstract: Canopy bulk density (CBD) data is essential for modeling the behavior of crown fires. Few studies generated spatially continuous CBD maps at landscape scale in China. This study developed a framework to estimate CBD using Chinese forest inventory data and multisource remote sensing imagery. We devised an indirect method for calculating plot level CBD based on the load-over-depth concept, integrating Chinese National Forest Inventory plots data and species-specific allometric equations. Pearson correlation and recursive feature elimination were used to identify optimal predictors for ensemble learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting. RF demonstrated the highest performance among these algorithms. The R 2 for the model were 0.67 and 0.57, respectively, and the RMSE values were 0.0219 kg/m 3 and 0.0269 kg/m 3 . The final 10-m resolution CBD map generated by the RF model for the study area, which revealed values ranging from 0.0180 to 0.1476 kg/m 3 , with a mean of 0.0808 kg/m 3 . Pixel-level uncertainty in spatial extrapolation was also quantified based on the RMSE and rRMSE. Additionally, explainable analysis identified the contribution of each selected feature. The accuracy of the resulting maps can serve as a baseline for the Chinese boreal forest.

title: Evaluation of minimal local recalibration for reducing transfer error in Sentinel-2 chlorophyll a estimation across heterogeneous waterbodies
abstract: Chlorophyll a (Chl a ) is a commonly used indicator of phytoplankton biomass, trophic status, and eutrophication risk in inland waters. Sentinel-2 satellite imagery can scale up spatiotemporal chlorophyll monitoring, but transferability of retrieval models across heterogeneous waterbodies remains a challenge for operational use. This study evaluated a local bias recalibration approach for Sentinel-2-based Chl a estimation in heterogeneous inland waters. The study covered 28 lakes and reservoirs in eastern Poland and included 203 field-satellite match-ups after quality control. Six modelling approaches were evaluated: 2 linear models, 2 generalized additive models, Elastic Net, and Random Forest. Transferability was assessed using leave-one-cluster-out cross-validation. A minimal recalibration of the bias component was tested using 0–3 reference samples. Transfer prediction errors were characterised using bias-scatter analysis. Without recalibration, generalized additive models and Random Forest showed the best transfer performance, with median RMSE of 0.270–0.274 and FAC2 of 69.05–71.43%. A single calibration sample significantly reduced transfer bias. For Linear (MCI), RMSE decreased from 0.377 to 0.190 and FAC2 increased from 35.42% to 85.71% from k = 0 to k = 1. The largest improvements were observed for simple linear models, while more complex models showed comparatively smaller gains. Recalibration mainly corrected systematic bias, with minimal effect on residual scatter. With 1–3 calibration points, simple models approached the performance of more complex models. Minimal local bias recalibration can effectively support Chl a monitoring in heterogeneous inland waters, particularly in systems that already rely on periodic in situ sampling.

title: Integrated effects of land-use change and human–environment interactions on habitat quality in the Chengdu–Chongqing urban agglomeration: Insights from explainable machine learning and structural equation modeling
abstract: The Chengdu–Chongqing urban agglomeration is a vital area in China's regional development plan and also plays an important role in protecting the environment. As the local economy expands rapidly, the ecosystem in this region is under growing pressure. However, limited research has examined the detailed evaluation of habitat quality (HQ) and the mechanisms underlying its evolution. This study applied the InVEST model, contribution index, and spatial autocorrelation analysis, combined with XGBoost–SHAP and a structural equation model (SEM), to systematically examine the spatiotemporal variations of HQ in the Chengdu–Chongqing region and its influencing factors. The findings indicate that: (1) Between 2000 and 2020, the HQ value in this region dropped from 0.615 to 0.606, indicating a small overall downward trend. (2) Ya'an and Leshan were important high-quality habitats, while Nanchong, Ziyang, Chengdu, and the main urban area of Chongqing were representative low-level habitats; spatially, low-level habitats in the central region gradually became fragmented, and high-quality habitats expanded eastward. (3) The ranking of the main influencing factors by their contribution was slope > temperature > cropland fragmentation > forestland fragmentation > vegetation greenness > nighttime illumination > population density. During the study period, urban expansion, cropland conversion, and changes in forest land configuration jointly altered the contribution of land-use structure to modeled HQ. (4) The SEM-based path analysis further showed that slope was linked to modeled HQ through vegetation greenness and land-use configuration. This study provides an extensive analysis of how climate, vegetation, landscape and human activities work together to affect HQ amid changes in land use. The findings provide practical evidence to help balance urban growth and ecological conservation as the Chengdu–Chongqing region undergoes rapid urbanization.

title: Time-series inversion of heavy metal and non-heavy metal water quality parameters and reveal their driving mechanisms using CNN-BiLSTM-Attention and PLS-SEM
abstract: Monitoring heavy metals and other pollution in drinking water sources is protecting public health, ensuring social stability, and promoting sustainable ecological development. Traditional fixed-point sampling approaches suffers from insufficient spatial coverage, weak remote sensing signals for heavy metals, and considerable challenges in achieving robust long-term inversion. To address these limitations, this study develops a multi-dimensional time-series feature fusion model (CNN-BiLSTM-Attention) for water quality parameter inversion. This model integrates a convolutional neural network (CNN), a bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM), and an attention mechanism to enable monthly inversion of eight indicators, including dissolved oxygen (DO), chemical oxygen demand (COD), ammonia nitrogen (NH₃-N), fluoride (F − ), permanganate (COD M n ), zinc (Zn), selenium (Se), and mercury (Hg). This paper investigates the spatiotemporal evolution of both heavy metal and non-heavy metal water quality parameters during normal, dry and flood seasons. A partial least squares structural equation model (PLS-SEM) is constructed to quantify the direct and indirect effects of climate, human activities, and hydrological characteristics on the dynamic changes of the eight water quality parameters, thereby identifying their dominant drivers. The results showed that the CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model substantially improves inversion performance by capturing nonlinear spatiotemporal relationships among water quality parameters (mean R 2 = 0.791), representing a 32.05% increase over the conventional CNN-LSTM model (mean R 2 = 0.599). From 2018 to 2024, the overall water quality exhibited an improving trend, with notable decreases in Hg, Zn, Se, and COD concentrations (maximum reduction of 68.3%), while DO and NH 3 -N increased slightly. Spatially, pollutants accumulated at the reservoir edge and tributary confluences during the dry season and migrated toward the reservoir center in the flood season. Notably, the low-DO area largely overlapped with the peak COD Mn and COD region in the southwestern tributary of the reservoir. PLS-SEM revealed that the organic pollution load (COD Mn , COD) serves as the central hub driving heavy metal evolution, exhibiting a strong positive correlation with heavy metal indicators (Hg, Se; β = 0.946, P < 0.001). Human activities exert a direct negative effect on oxygen-consuming pollutants (DO, NH₃-N; β = −0.359, P < 0.01) and indirectly modulate heavy metal dynamics through the organic pollution load pathway ( β = −0.432, P < 0.05). Climatic factors (primarily rainfall, β = 0.534, P < 0.1) and water temperature ( β = −0.562, P < 0.05) constitute the dynamic basis of heavy metal evolution. The proposed time-series inversion and driving mechanism analysis method enables both temporal monitoring and attribution analysis of heavy metals and non-heavy metals in water bodies, providing reliable scientific support for water quality management in drinking water sources.

title: Assessing the cross-scale spillover effect of urban Heat Island (UHI): an indicator-based approach in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region
abstract: Due to rapid urbanization, urban heat island (UHI) effects have expanded from city-level phenomena to continuous cross-city UHI belts, posing challenges to regional ecological security and public health. However, a critical research gap remains: the spatial structure, formation mechanisms, and cross-scale transmission processes of continuous UHI belts are insufficiently quantified, primarily due to a reliance on isolated, single-scale analyses. In this study, an indicator-based, multiscale analytical framework was developed at the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei (BTH) region, city, and 1-km grid scales. Landscape metrics, a coupled random forest-geographic SHAP (RF-GeoSHAP) model, and generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs) were used to investigate the hierarchical transmission pathways of continuous UHI belts. Our results show that these belts emerge as structurally connected regional heat sources once heat island dominance (HID) surpasses a nonlinear threshold of approximately 7%. At the agglomeration scale, HID, along with climatic and ecological backgrounds (PRE, NDVI, TMP), are identified as the dominant thermal predictors, while at the fine grid scale, local thermal accumulation is substantially amplified by building height (BH) and sky view factor (SVF) under structural forcing. Crucially, the influence of these key driving indicators exhibits clear threshold effects that are nonlinearly amplified by regional UHI connectivity. Overall, this study enhances the understanding of UHI dynamics across scales and offers valuable insights for indicator-guided UHI mitigation strategies at the urban agglomeration scale.

title: Spatially non-stationary and threshold-dependent drivers of cropland productivity in humid subtropical China revealed by explainable machine learning
abstract: Understanding spatially heterogeneous controls on cropland productivity is critical for improving agroecosystem sustainability under increasing climatic variability and anthropogenic pressure. However, the nonlinear and spatially non-stationary relationships between productivity and its drivers remain difficult to quantify using conventional approaches. Using multi-source remote sensing and ancillary datasets, this study applied an interpretable machine-learning approach to investigate the spatial controls of cropland net primary productivity (NPP) across humid subtropical China based on two representative periods (2010 and 2020). Results showed that cropland NPP increased by 4.7% during the study period, although substantial spatial heterogeneity persisted. Climatic factors, particularly potential evapotranspiration and mean annual temperature, showed the strongest contributions to spatial variations in NPP, with their contribution patterns exhibiting pronounced spatial reversals along hydroclimatic gradients. Soil pH acted as a conditional regulator within a narrow optimal range (5.5–6.0), whereas nitrogen fertilizer input and population density imposed increasingly negative effects beyond critical thresholds. Clustering of pixel-level SHAP vectors identified four functional zones characterized by distinct combinations of dominant drivers and constraint regimes, linking regional productivity gains with localized vulnerability risks. The results further reveal that cropland productivity exhibits multiple interacting constraint domains, where productivity responses depend on whether local conditions remain within effective threshold ranges. By integrating remote sensing observations with explainable machine learning, this study provides a spatially explicit framework for understanding productivity–ecological environment relationships and supporting adaptive cropland management under climate change.

title: Long-term multi-source remote sensing reveals region-specific driving mechanisms of forest fire spatiotemporal patterns across floristic sub-regions in mountainous Yunnan, China
abstract: Sharp gradients in floristic composition, fuel productivity, hydrothermal conditions and human accessibility can reshape forest fire disturbance in mountain regions, but administrative analyses may obscure ecological differences among vegetation regions. Using Yunnan Province, this study integrated Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer Terra thermal-anomaly product (MOD14A1), Fire Climate Change Initiative version 5.1 (FireCCI51), Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS), Landsat and Sentinel-2 data for 2006–2025. A Simple Non-Iterative Clustering–Random Forest (SNIC–RF) framework mapped burned areas at 30 m resolution. Burned-area maps were summarised across eight floristic sub-regions using a four-dimensional fire-disturbance indicator matrix, including fire timing, burned area, fire-event number and reburned extent. Climatic, vegetation, topographic and human-activity variables were analysed using 5 km × 5 km grids and eXtreme Gradient Boosting–SHapley Additive exPlanations (XGBoost–SHAP). The SNIC–RF framework showed stable performance, with mean Overall Accuracy (OA) and burned-class F1-score values of 91.391% and 85.391%. Forest fires fluctuated strongly, with burned area peaking in 2010 and reaching a secondary high in 2023. Fire-event numbers were high in 2010, 2012–2014 and 2023, but were not synchronised with burned area, indicating joint controls from occurrence pressure and fire-spread size. Single-burn disturbances dominated, whereas Regions I, VII and VIII had more dispersed burn-frequency structures. At the provincial scale, mean temperature (TEM) was the strongest driver, followed by soil moisture (SM) and wind speed (VS). Across floristic sub-regions, TEM remained the common control, while gross primary productivity (GPP), digital elevation model (DEM), VS and SM acted as regional modifiers, and precipitation (PRE), population density (PD) and topographic wetness index (TWI) showed local enhancement. These findings indicate that floristic sub-regions are ecologically meaningful units for explaining regional fire heterogeneity and mechanism reorganisation, and can support the construction of sub-region-based fire-disturbance indicators, the identification of reburning-prone areas, differentiated fire-risk zoning and post-fire restoration prioritisation in mountain landscapes.

title: The impact of extreme climate events on carbon and water fluxes in grassland ecosystems on the Qinghai-Xizang plateau
abstract: The Qinghai-Xizang Plateau (QXP) plays a crucial role in regulating terrestrial carbon and water exchanges. However, the impacts of increasingly frequent extreme climate events on ecosystem carbon and water fluxes remain insufficiently understood. Here, machine learning models using multi-source datasets were applied to simulate gross primary productivity (GPP) and evapotranspiration (ET) across QXP grassland ecosystems from 1958 to 2024 and to quantify their responses to extreme climate events. Results showed that: (1) the random forest model outperformed other models and revealed significant increasing trends in both GPP and ET; (2) carbon and water fluxes were generally positively correlated with warm extremes, negatively correlated with cold extremes, and showed predominantly negative responses to precipitation-related extremes; and (3) cold compound events (cold/dry and cold/wet) posed the greatest risk to carbon-water cycling, whereas hot compound events exerted weaker impacts on GPP but increased water consumption. Overall, QXP grassland carbon and water fluxes were most vulnerable to cold compound events. These findings improve understanding of alpine grassland responses to climate extremes and provide a scientific basis for ecosystem management under future climate change.

title: Research on attribution and prediction of runoff changes in loess gully areas based on SWAT and machine learning models
abstract: Runoff evolution is a key issue affecting regional ecological security and the sustainable utilization of water and soil resources in loess gully regions. The Rui River Basin (RRB) was selected as the study area, and a research framework of trend testing, model coupling, attribution analysis and scenario prediction was constructed, and temporal evolution pattern of runoff was systematically revealed. Based on the SWAT model and its output data, an XGBoost quantile regression (XGBoost-QR) model was developed for runoff simulation comparison, demonstrating the advantages of integrating physical mechanisms with machine learning models, and the contribution of climate change and human activities to runoff changes were quantified using the scenario separation method. Finally, integrating the CMIP6 (BCC-CSM2-MR) climate scenarios and predictions of land use and land cover change (LUCC) patterns were incorporated into the SWAT model, runoff trends from 2022 to 2040 were predicted. The results showed that: (1) Precipitation at Huating (HT), Ankou (AK), and Yuanjiaan (YJA) increased (6.60–10.50 mm/10a), whereas annual runoff generally decreased (0.004–0.04 × 10 8 m 3 /10a), with abrupt changes occurring in 1990 and 2009. (2) The coupling model enhanced the overall simulation accuracy, human interventions were generally the dominant factor driving runoff changes, contributing 42.86% ∼ 73.69%, while the contribution rate of LUCC was between 16.67% and 45.71%. (3) From 2022 to 2040, annual runoff shows an increasing trend (0.01–0.44 m 3 /s·10a) under SSP1–2.6, SSP2–4.5, and SSP5–8.5. Through multi-model integration and multi-scenario analysis, this study provides a scientific basis for the coordinated regulation of water and soil resources and ecological adaptive management in loess gully regions.

title: A remote sensing-based tree mortality indicator for biodiversity monitoring using multispectral UAV and lidar in the Arctic region, Finland
abstract: Deadwood is a recognised ecological indicator for forest biodiversity. Both the UN Convention on Biological Diversity and the EU Biodiversity Strategy 2030 mandates inventorying and reporting deadwood. However, monitoring tree mortality, the source of deadwood, remains challenging, especially in Arctic and sub-Arctic regions. Boreal forests in this region face increasing climate-driven stressors: droughts, pest outbreaks, and snow damage. These stressors accelerate tree mortality and threaten biodiversity. Deep learning-based semantic segmentation offers a scalable solution for monitoring standing tree mortality using remote sensing data such as multispectral UAV imagery and lidar-derived canopy height models. In this study, we (1) evaluated a U-Net model for detecting tree mortality across 208 ha of Picea abies , Pinus sylvestris , and deciduous dominated forests, and (2) produced a wall-to-wall mortality map to identify spatial patterns and potential drivers in Northern Lapland, Finland. The training dataset included 411 tiles containing 4380 manually delineated tree crowns. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 0.92, with a recall and F1-score for dead trees 0.82 and 0.57, for alive trees 0.93 and 0.96. The performance is sufficient for identifying spatial patterns despite false positive detections. Mortality hotspots were concentrated in Picea abies dominated areas at higher elevations where older trees were located, suggesting a link to snow damage besides natural mortality. These results demonstrate the potential of UAV based deep learning workflows for large-scale exploratory monitoring of tree mortality patterns in northern boreal forests in Arctic and sub-Arctic region and supports biodiversity reporting and restoration monitoring through spatial forest-health assessment.

title: Revealing the alterations of social-ecological system networks by China's national parks: Evidence from the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, China
abstract: National parks are pivotal instruments for advancing biodiversity conservation and fostering regional sustainable development. Yet, against the backdrop of intensifying climate change and growing anthropogenic pressures, the mechanisms by which national park governance reshapes coupled social-ecological systems (SES) remain insufficiently elucidated. Taking Qinghai Province, China, as a case study, this research integrates multi-source data to systematically investigate county-level ecological dynamics from 2005 to 2023. We employed a mixed-methods framework combining social network analysis (SNA), machine learning, and partial least squares structural equation modeling to quantify spatiotemporal variations in ecological importance, trace the dynamic evolution of SES linkage networks, and disentangle the direct and indirect pathways through which natural and anthropogenic factors drive SES dynamics. The results indicate that the evolution of SES shows a general trend of growing connectivity and stronger coupling. The linkage between economic and ecological components is positively shaped by a topography-soil-vegetation cascade, with standardized path coefficients of 0.72, 0.73, and 0.90, respectively. Compared with non-park areas, national park areas showed enhanced network structural cohesion, with policy-induced increases of 40% in network density, 35.16% in average clustering coefficient, and 70.89% in average weighted degree. Meanwhile, natural processes contribute to a more notable rise in coupling intensity. These findings advance the theoretical understanding of the socio-ecological impacts of protected area governance and provide a rigorous scientific basis for guiding the sustainable transition toward integrated ecological protection and socio-economic development at the regional scale.

title: An interpretable–causal learning framework for identifying the drivers of surface urban Heat Island intensity: evidence from 527 urban clusters in China
abstract: Under the combined effects of global warming and rapid urbanization, urban morphology has emerged as an important factor associated with variations in surface urban heat island intensity (SUHII) through its influence on surface physical properties and urban energy balance. Ho，wever, existing studies have largely relied on statistical correlation analyses and often lack standardized definitions of reference zones or sufficient control of confounding variables, making it challenging to disentangle environmental disturbances and identify the underlying drivers of SUHII and their spatial variability. To address these limitations, this study employs the Google Earth Engine platform to construct a multi-constraint framework for quantifying SUHII across 527 urban clusters in China and integrates LightGBM-SHAP with Double Machine Learning (DML) to establish an analytical framework that combines correlation analysis, causal inference, and mechanism interpretation. The results indicate pronounced spatial heterogeneity in summer daytime SUHII across China, with generally higher values observed in eastern and southern regions than in western and northern regions. Correlation analysis identifies impervious surface fraction (ISF) and tree canopy cover (PT) as the dominant statistical predictors. However, causal inference suggests that ISF (ATE = 0.374), largest patch index (LPI, ATE = 0.253), and water body proportion (PW, ATE = −0.240) exhibit relatively robust average estimated effects within the causal inference framework at the national scale. By contrast, PT, building height (BH), and patch density (PD) display substantial contextual dependence, with their thermal regulation effects varying across different climatic conditions, which may explain their inconsistent significance within the causal framework. By integrating correlation-based identification with causal validation, this study helps clarify the scope and limitations of urban morphological influences on SUHII and provides scientific support for the development of differentiated and evidence-informed urban planning strategies aimed at improving climate resilience.

title: Total suspended matter dynamics in the Songhua River over four decades: evidence of anthropogenic decoupling between soil erosion and in-stream regulation
abstract: Human activities have profoundly altered suspended-sediment dynamics in large rivers; however, long-term, spatially explicit records that disentangle basin-wide forcing from reach-specific engineering impacts remain scarce. Here, we develop a Random Forest (RF) retrieval model based on Landsat top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance and 542 in situ samples to reconstruct annual Total Suspended Matter (TSM) concentrations along the main stem of the Songhua River from 1984 to 2023. The resulting four-decade record reveals a basin-wide decline beginning in the early 1990s, accompanied by pronounced spatial heterogeneity among river reaches. At the basin scale, the relationship between watershed soil erosion (RUSLE-based dataset, 1990–2022) and riverine TSM is weak at the annual timescale. This weaken the linkage is most evident in the SRH–FRH reach downstream of the Dadingzishan hydro-junction, where in-stream regulation may override upstream erosion signals. Breakpoint analysis, using 2008 as the full-impoundment year, indicates a marked acceleration in TSM decline within SRH–FRH, from −0.22 mg L −1 yr −1 during 1984–2008 to −0.78 mg L −1 yr −1 during 2009–2023. A reach-to-reach quasi-experimental comparison further demonstrates a significant post-2008 divergence between SRH–FRH and a downstream control reach (ANOVA: F = 13.045, p = 0.0001), reinforcing the interpretation that reservoir regulation exerted a dominant, reach-specific influence on suspended sediment dynamics after impoundment. Together, these findings indicate that in heavily managed basins, in-stream engineering can reorganize sediment connectivity and partially weaken the linkage between downstream suspended sediment from basin-scale erosion signals. This process underscores the need to explicitly incorporate reservoir operation into sediment management and water-quality governance frameworks.

title: Threshold-governed nonlinearities and configurational interactions of development activities on cultural landscape resilience in karst traditional villages
abstract: In mountainous regions, traditional villages face deepening tensions between cultural landscape conservation and economic development. Various development activities' impacts on Cultural Landscape Resilience (CLR) exhibit complex nonlinearities and uncharted configurational effects. This study examines 636 village-year observations from 106 karst traditional villages in Southwest China (2020–2025), using gradient boosting regression trees and configurational analysis. Results demonstrate threshold-governed nonlinearities in individual activities: tourism investment, infrastructure improvement, road expansion, public service facilities investment, and agricultural facilities investment emerge as high-importance predictors, following four distinct patterns, optimal-intensity saturation, dual-critical-point transition, discrete-threshold activation, and path-dependent lock-in. For combinational effects, tourism and infrastructure investments serve as primary interaction hubs, capable of forming strong interactions with multiple development activities and influencing CLR. Moderate-intensity configurations (M-M, M-L, L-M) generate positive CLR outcomes through synergistic mechanisms, whereas extreme configurations ( L − L , H − L , L − H ) produce antagonistic effects. These findings advance a precision governance framework grounded in dynamic intensity thresholds and evidence-based synergy strategies.

title: Quantifying driving mechanisms and spatial optimization of water supply-demand dynamics in humid subtropical regions: Evidence from a typical hilly region of southern China (1996–2023)
abstract: Humid regions, traditionally regarded as relatively water-abundant, are increasingly facing localized water scarcity and spatial mismatches between water supply and demand under the combined pressures of rapid urbanization, industrial agglomeration, and climate change. This study focused on Jiangxi Province, a representative humid subtropical region in China. We developed an integrated analytical framework by coupling the InVEST model, bivariate spatial autocorrelation analysis, and XGBoost-SHAP interpretable machine learning. This framework was used to systematically examine the spatiotemporal dynamics of regional water supply (WS) and water demand (WD) from 1996 to 2023, identify spatial clustering patterns, quantify key influencing factors and their spatially heterogeneous model-based contributions, and delineate differentiated water-resource management zones. The results showed that: (1) Jiangxi Province generally remained in a water-surplus condition during 1996–2023, with a mean water security index (WSI) of 0.36; however, WD increased by 21.57%, far exceeding the increase in WS of 2.21%. The spatial distributions of regional water supply and demand exhibited a relatively stable pattern characterized by long-term supply–demand surplus in mountainous areas and intensifying imbalance in the northern plain. (2) based on a two-dimensional zoning framework integrating WSI surplus–deficit status and spatial clustering patterns, the study area was divided into five functional zones, and corresponding management strategies were proposed for each zone. (3) gross domestic product (GDP) and precipitation (PRE) were the most important contributing factors associated with WSI. The negative contribution of GDP was most pronounced in the urban agglomerations of the northern plain, whereas the positive contributions of PRE, slope, and plant available water content (PAWC) were concentrated in the eastern and southern mountainous areas, highlighting the spatially heterogeneous associations of natural endowments and human activities with WSI. This study provides a transferable methodological reference for identifying water supply–demand mismatches, diagnosing WSI, formulating differentiated management strategies, and the understanding of driving mechanisms in humid subtropical regions

title: Interpretable deep-learning assessment of environmental indicators of global marine plastic pollution across ocean basins and climate zones
abstract: Marine plastic pollution has emerged as a pressing global environmental issue and poses a significant threat to both oceanic ecosystems and human well-being. Nevertheless, the patterns of its dispersion and the environmental associations underlying its distribution remain inadequately characterized on a worldwide scale, primarily due to the limitations of traditional monitoring and modeling techniques. In this study, we introduced an interpretable deep learning (DL) framework to predict the plastic pollution level across global oceans and to elucidate the model-attributed environmental associations. Multiple global datasets of plastic pollution concentrations and relevant environmental variables from 2018 to 2022 were integrated. A total of 1193 surface-ocean records were initially compiled. After harmonization and quality control, 1155 records were retained for model development, including 916 training samples and 239 samples in a held-out internal test set. The predictive performance of the FCNN was benchmarked against several widely used machine-learning models. Although XGBoost achieved the highest predictive accuracy and was identified as the best-performing benchmark model, the FCNN demonstrated competitive predictive performance and was retained as the focal deep-learning architecture for evaluating the proposed interpretable neural-network framework. The FCNN model demonstrated moderate predictive performance under random internal validation based on 13 environmental predictor variables spanning geographic, biological, biogeochemical, physicochemical, physical-dynamic, and transport-related categories, achieving a mean five-fold cross-validation R 2 of 0.608 and a held-out internal test-set R 2 of 0.612. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis identified DTC, dissolved oxygen, net primary productivity, and phytoplankton concentration as the main environmental indicators contributing to model predictions. Stratification analysis further revealed distinct regional differences in model-attribution patterns and predictor importance across the four major ocean basins (Atlantic, Pacific, Indian, and Arctic) and climate zones (tropical, temperate, and polar), thereby emphasizing the necessity for region-specific management strategies. This interpretable DL framework provides a data-driven approach for large-scale marine plastic pollution assessment and regional monitoring support within the range of environmental conditions represented by the available data.

title: Topography-human activities-climate jointly shape the multi-scale spatiotemporal patterns of alpine ecosystem services: Evidence from the Zoige Plateau, China
abstract: Alpine ecosystems serve as critical bulwarks for regional ecological security and provide irreplaceable ecosystem services (ESs). However, the multi-scale interactions among ESs and their coupled natural-human driving mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering targeted improvements and collaborative management of ecological functions. This study quantified the spatiotemporal dynamics, trade-offs/synergies, and bundles of four key ESs (carbon storage (CS), habitat quality (HQ), soil conservation (SC), and water yield (WY)) across different scales in China's Zoige Plateau. XGBoost-SHAP machine learning and structural equation modeling (SEM) were used to explore the impacts of topography, climate, and human activities on ESs and their driving pathways. The results revealed the following: (1) Across the three observation years, WY and SC were higher in 2020 than in 2000, whereas CS and HQ showed lower values in 2020. Spatially, WY was higher in the south and lower in the north; high values of CS and HQ were concentrated in the marsh wetlands and forests. (2) Significant trade-offs and synergies existed among ESs. HQ showed synergistic relationships with CS and SC, while WY exhibited trade-offs with CS and HQ, with evident scale effects. Multi-scale ES bundles displayed clear spatial differentiation. (3) Machine learning identified precipitation (PRE) dominated changes in WY, slope significantly promoted SC, and elevation (DEM) contributed the most to CS and HQ. SEM further indicated that DEM directly influenced PRE, potential evapotranspiration (PET), and the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), thereby establishing the natural supply base for ESs. Meanwhile, gross domestic product (GDP) acted as an intermediate regulatory factor, significantly mediating the conversion efficiency of these three variables into ESs. This study reveals a nonlinear coupling mechanism in which topography, climate, and socio-economic regulatory factors synergistically shape ESs, providing scientific support for differentiated zoning, synergistic optimization, and sustainable management of alpine ecosystems.

title: Opportunity or challenge? Exploring the impact of artificial intelligence on climate change adaptive capacity
abstract: Climate change is expected to negatively impact countries worldwide, but the adaptive responses of different nations to this threat vary significantly. Efforts to enhance adaptive capacity to climate change have been largely insufficient. This paper aims to explore how to make use of artificial intelligence to enhance the adaptive capacity to climate change by using a dataset spanning 66 countries. This paper first finds a positive link between artificial intelligence and climate change adaptive capacity, showing that artificial intelligence significantly boosts adaptive capacity to climate change. Furthermore, artificial intelligence enhances climate change adaptive capacity across all areas, from infrastructure adaptability to ecosystem services adaptability. Third, this paper confirms a significant moderating effect of climate aid. Climate aid amplifies artificial intelligence's effectiveness in enhancing climate change adaptive capacity, highlighting a synergistic interaction. Fourth, we identify natural disaster losses and productivity as major channels through which artificial intelligence impacts climate change adaptive capacity. In addition, impact channels vary by income levels: in low-income countries, artificial intelligence facilitates the development of energy infrastructure, whereas in high-income countries, artificial intelligence supports energy transition, leading to higher climate change adaptive capacity levels. Based on these findings, we propose several policy implications to enhance AI-driven climate adaptation, scale up climate aid effectiveness, and tailor energy pathways according to country income levels.

title: Assessing the impact of natural environment and human activities on the ecological environmental quality based on RSEI in Inner Mongolia from 2000 to 2020
abstract: The ecological environment quality of Inner Mongolia is a fundamental pillar for sustaining regional environmental health and safeguarding human well-being. Despite its critical importance, the region has faced escalating ecological challenges in recent years, yet the dynamics of its ecosystems and the underlying drivers of change remain largely underexplored. This study aims to assess the ecological environment quality in Inner Mongolia and investigate the impacts of a total of seventeen natural and human factors using remote sensing data and machine learning. The remote sensing ecological index (RSEI) was used to reveal the ecological environment quality and its spatiotemporal variation from 2000 to 2020 was analyzed. An interpretable machine learning framework, integrating Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) with eXtreme Gradient Boosting Trees (XGBoost), was then employed to uncover the complex driving mechanisms influencing the ecological environment quality. The results reveal a slight but clear improving trend in the ecological environment quality over the two decades, accompanied by pronounced spatial heterogeneity. Notably, net improvement is characterized by significant expansion of moderate and good areas, alongside contraction of poor and worst areas. The XGBoost-SHAP model identifies climatic factors as primary drivers, with precipitation as the most influential positive factor (exceeding 273.79 mm), while temperature variables act as dominant negative factors (suppressing the ecological environment quality beyond 3.02 °C and 11.71 °C). Relationships are predominantly nonlinear with critical thresholds. Interaction analysis further indicates that any single factor's effect highly depends on other factors. Crucially, these findings demonstrate that the overarching regional vegetation recovery is fundamentally a climate-driven process, wherein anthropogenic restoration efforts play a secondary role. By elucidating these nonlinear and threshold-dependent mechanisms, this study provides a robust, transferable basis for targeted ecological restoration and management strategies, offering critical insights for arid ecosystems in Inner Mongolia and globally.

title: Response of vegetation ecological water requirement to landscape evolution: From non-linear regulation to critical sensitive zones
abstract: The intensification of global environmental change has accelerated the reorganization of terrestrial landscapes. Such structural variations inevitably alter local climatic conditions and ecosystem functions, thereby governing the spatiotemporal distribution of ecological water requirement (EWR). However, the non-linear constraining effects of landscape spatial configuration on vegetation EWR remain underexplored. This study characterized landscape pattern evolution in the Ziya River Basin (ZYRB) and applied a SHAP-interpreted random forest model to decouple its regulatory effects on EWR. Furthermore, a comprehensive framework for sensitivity analysis was developed to identify critical thresholds and sensitive zones. Results indicated a distinct trend toward landscape fragmentation and diversification from 1990 to 2023. The increased patch fragmentation, shape complexity, and diversity, particularly the Fractal Dimension Index ( r = −0.73) was associated with reduced EWR, whereas heightened structural connectivity amplified water demand. Spatially, climatic factors dominated the heterogeneity of EWR, accounting for about 64% of the total importance. Among the landscape pattern indices, the Fractal Dimension Index (FRAC) and Patch Cohesion Index (COHESION) emerged as the leading modulators, with each explaining approximately 9% of the total variance. The response of EWR to landscape drivers exhibited the U-shaped or fluctuating trends rather than simple linearity. The meteorologically sensitive zones identified based on the thresholds were predominantly concentrated in mountain-plain ecotones and groundwater over-exploited regions distributed along a northeast-southwest strip extending across eastern Shijiazhuang and central Handan City. Landscape -sensitive zones coincided with regions of high structural complexity, which were clustered in the western parts of Shijiazhuang and Xingtai City, as well as in Yangquan City. These insights underscore the critical role of landscape complexity in buffering water stress and provide the spatially explicit scientific basis for formulating water regulation measures and land management strategies. The proposed framework possesses broad applicability for diagnosing constraint mechanisms and delineating critical zones in diverse ecological contexts.

title: Cross-scale hotspot transition and scale-dependent drivers of urban bird richness
abstract: Biodiversity conservation has become a major challenge in rapidly urbanizing regions, where environmental heterogeneity reshapes ecological patterns across spatial and seasonal dimensions. However, most studies have focused on identifying a single optimal scale while overlooking how biodiversity responses vary across scales. In this study, we developed an integrated framework combining multi-scale analysis, explainable machine learning, and seasonal simulations to investigate urban bird diversity patterns in Shenzhen, China. More than 215,000 citizen-science bird records and environmental variables were analyzed across spatial scales ranging from 300 m to 2000 m. The results revealed strong scale dependency in both model performance and environmental responses. Among all scales, 1000 m achieved the highest predictive accuracy and ecological interpretability, representing the optimal scale for modeling urban bird diversity. Cross-scale hotspot analysis identified stable, attenuated, and emergent hotspot transition patterns, indicating that biodiversity-supporting conditions undergo persistence, attenuation, and spatial reorganization during scaling processes. Environmental drivers exhibited hierarchical shifts across scales, transitioning from fine-scale habitat regulation to broader climatic, topographic, and anthropogenic control, accompanied by widespread nonlinear threshold responses. Seasonal simulations further revealed substantial temporal shifts in hotspot distributions and driver dominance associated with species phenology. Overall, this study provides a scale-adaptive framework for understanding urban biodiversity responses and offers practical implications for ecological monitoring, biodiversity conservation, and spatial planning in rapidly urbanizing landscapes.
