title: Fusing UAV-LiDAR, yield-table inversion, and Sentinel data for forest aboveground biomass stock and increment mapping with Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation
abstract: Accurate mapping of forest carbon stocks and their future dynamics is critical for carbon cycle assessment, national greenhouse gas reporting, and forest carbon credit verification, yet most remote sensing approaches provide only static snapshots. This study develops a pipeline integrating individual-tree UAV-LiDAR analytics, yield-table inversion, machine learning, and multi-source satellite imagery to produce 10 m resolution maps of aboveground carbon stocks and projected carbon increments across Shikoku Island, Japan. Tree age and site quality were estimated for 132,890 trees by inverting the Local Yield table Construction System (LYCS) using LiDAR-derived height and diameter at breast height (DBH). An XGBoost model incorporating LYCS-derived age, site quality, topography, and species achieved an individual-tree aboveground biomass (AGB) R 2 of 0.86. AGB was converted to carbon stock using a uniform carbon fraction of 0.47 for model extrapolation. Forward age projection generated carbon increment maps at 5-, 10-, and 20-year horizons whose annual increments followed the ecologically expected rise, mid-rotation peak and decline. Satellite upscaling using Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and DEM features achieved a stock model R 2 of 0.74 (rRMSE = 25.1%) under random hold-out validation, decreasing to 0.49 and 0.41 under spatial block and leave-one-survey-area-out validation, so the hold-out values describe within-domain performance. Separate carbon change models trained on Sentinel-1/2 features achieved hold-out R 2 of 0.69–0.74 (0.37–0.52 under the spatially independent schemes). Compared with GEDI L4B over a common forest domain, the estimates were higher by +25.8 Mg ha −1 . A Monte Carlo budget following IPCC Approach 1, propagating age and site quality jointly through the biomass model, gave total uncertainties of 48.5, 46.7 and 42.4% for the 5-, 10- and 20-year extrapolated maps. The outputs could support the monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) workflows of Japan's J-Credit Scheme and international voluntary carbon market standards as an exploratory decision-support and spatial-stratification tool.

title: Rethinking pathways of ecological management: Insights from climate-driven ecosystem health
abstract: Translating multidimensional ecosystem-health assessment into climate-sensitive management remains challenging in arid regions. Taking Xinjiang, China, as a representative desert-oasis-mountain system, this study developed a research framework comprising separate modules for VORS-based Ecosystem Health Index (EHI) assessment, LSTM time-series projection, climate-EHI LSTM-SHAP analysis, and management zoning. EHI was assessed at five-year intervals from 1990 to 2020 and projected to 2035 using historical EHI sequences. Model selection employed temporally blocked validation, with 2020 retained as an independent test set. Across five runs, LSTM outperformed linear regression and Random Forest. Spatially, relatively high EHI values were concentrated in the Altay, Tianshan, and Kunlun Mountains, whereas the Junggar and Tarim basins were dominated by low-to-moderate health levels. Historical changes were generally small and spatially heterogeneous, with localized improvement and degradation coexisting across Xinjiang. A separate climate-EHI LSTM-SHAP analysis identified precipitation of the wettest quarter, precipitation of the warmest quarter, and annual precipitation as the most influential climatic variables and revealed nonlinear, variable-specific response ranges. The nine selected climatic variables were used to construct the Ecosystem Climate Sensitivity Index (ECS), which was coupled with EHI to delineate five mutually exclusive management zones. The resulting zoning distinguishes priorities for ecological intervention, climate-sensitive regulation, early warning, functional maintenance, and coordinated conservation and enhancement.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and future trends in vegetation productivity in Xinjiang driven by vapor pressure deficit and potential evapotranspiration
abstract: Under climate change, extreme drought events have become increasingly frequent; however, the regulatory mechanisms through which atmospheric drought affects vegetation productivity in arid regions remain unclear. Understanding the spatiotemporal relationships between vegetation productivity, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), and potential evapotranspiration (PET) is essential for assessing ecosystem responses to climate change. Using remote-sensing normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), gross primary productivity (GPP), and meteorological VPD and PET data for Xinjiang from 2004 to 2023, this study employed trend analysis, the Hurst exponent, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) to investigate vegetation responses to atmospheric drought stress and the persistence of future trends. GPP increased significantly in 22% of the study area and NDVI in 8.9%, mainly along the Tarim Basin margins, whereas localized vegetation degradation occurred in northern Xinjiang. VPD and PET were primary statistical contributors, with substantially higher relative importance than other factors. Temporally, both were negatively correlated with vegetation productivity; spatially, positive correlations occurred in southern oasis regions, whereas negative correlations predominated in northern Xinjiang. Strong temporal persistence in vegetation productivity was observed in only 8.6% of the vegetated areas. GPP is projected to decline after peaking in 2019, reaching approximately 197.62 g C m −2 yr −1 by 2033, while XGBoost achieved relatively high predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.78). Overall, atmospheric drought substantially constrained vegetation productivity and weakened ecosystem stability, highlighting the need for differentiated management strategies in southern and northern Xinjiang to mitigate the risk of regional vegetation productivity decline.

title: Multi-objective optimization of “human-grassland-wild ungulate-livestock” system in a typical nature reserve on the Qinghai-Tibetan plateau
abstract: Nature reserves on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau (QTP) play crucial roles in supporting ecological security. Achieving the balance of “human-grassland-wild ungulate-livestock” (HGWL) system is important for sustainable development in these nature reserves. This study developed an indicator-based decision-support framework based on machine learning (ML) methods and the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) in the Changtang Nature Reserve on the QTP. An extreme gradient boosting model was employed to quantify the imbalance between aboveground biomass (AGB) and crude protein (CP) required by livestock and wild ungulates and that supplied by grasslands. A multi-objective optimization model of HGWL system aiming to increase the ecological and economic benefits and decrease the grassland pressure was constructed using NSGA-II based on the imbalance of AGB and CP. This model was applied to analyze the optimized cultivated grasslands planting structure, livestock structure and other variables in three scenarios. Ecological benefits decreased by 0.50% in economic development priority scenario, and economic benefits decreased by 16.22% in ecological protection priority scenario. By contrast, ecological benefits and economic benefits increased, and grassland pressure decreased by 5.06%, 5.05%, and 0.74% respectively in ecological economic balance scenario, which was identified as the optimal scenario. More areas of alfalfa, higher sheep slaughter volume and lower goat and yak slaughter volume were recommended to achieve the HGWL balance. The combination of ML and NSGA-II can help achieve the multi-objective optimization of HGWL system, and this framework has potential to be promoted to other nature reserves around the world.

title: Improving multi-factor river water quality prediction using deep learning and large language models with retrieval-augmented generation
abstract: Water quality prediction is critical to protect river ecosystems and sustain effective water management under increasing urbanization pressures. Current methods rely on a limited number of influencing factors and lack interpretability, which presents challenges in practical applications. Emerging large language models (LLMs) have strong capabilities for understanding domain knowledge, but require most relevant information for reliability. This study proposed an automated multi-factor river water quality prediction framework by coupling deep learning with LLMs enhanced by retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). A multi-dimensional dataset was constructed by integrating water quality with meteorological, socio-economic and hydro-topographic features to fully characterize river dynamics. Then, LLM-guided hybrid deep learning model, combining convolutional neural network (CNN), long short-term memory (LSTM) and attention mechanisms, namely LCLA model, was developed to predict six water quality indicators. Hyperparameters covering model structure and training strategy were efficiently configured through a literature-based knowledge retrieval, achieving optimal MAE, MSE, RMSE, and MAPE of 0.42, 0.96, 0.54, and 0.11, respectively, with improved optimization efficiency. Model interpretability was enhanced using Shapley analysis, revealing main contributions of turbidity, domestic water use, and river discharge. Finally, a RAG-enhanced multi-agent system was established to perform water quality grade classification and improvement recommendation generation by integrating domain knowledge and expert experience with LLM reasoning. The case study of Xinwu District demonstrated actionable management guidance consistent with on-site conditions. This study offered a reliable and efficient framework, with advantages in prediction performance and knowledge decision support, for advancing intelligent river water quality prediction and management in complex environments.

title: Assessing plastic-related environmental risk across EU countries of the Danube basin using a composite risk index
abstract: Plastic-related environmental risk in transboundary river systems represents a multidimensional challenge emerging from the interaction between plastic-related pressures, the vulnerability of receiving aquatic environments, and the capacity of circular economy systems to mitigate environmental impacts. This study investigates the structural factors associated with plastic-related environmental risk and the resulting territorial configurations across seven European Union countries of the Danube basin. Using a balanced panel dataset comprising 84 country-year observations for seven European Union countries over the period 2012–2023, the study develops the Danube Plastic-related Pollution Risk Index (DPPRI), a composite indicator that operationalizes plastic-related environmental risk through the integration of plastic-related pressure, organic pollution vulnerability, and circular economy mitigation capacity. The analytical framework combines composite indicator construction, an Ordinary Least Squares benchmark, supervised machine learning, model interpretation, and unsupervised clustering. Random Forest modelling is applied to assess the relative contribution of environmental, economic, and circular-economy indicators to modelled DPPRI variability, while SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis identifies the magnitude and direction of each indicator's contribution to the predicted composite-index values. K-means clustering, supported by an exploratory hierarchical clustering assessment, is further employed to identify structural risk typologies among the 84 country-year observations. The results show that trade-related plastic flows, the operationalized environmental vulnerability dimension, and indicators of circular-economy intensity and decoupling are among the principal factors associated with variability in the composite risk index, while recycling and recovery performance contribute to the mitigation dimension of the framework. The clustering analysis identifies three distinct structural risk profiles among the analysed country-year observations, reflecting different combinations of plastic-related pressure, environmental vulnerability, economic activity, and mitigation capacity. This study contributes an integrated and potentially transferable risk-screening framework for examining structural conditions associated with plastic-related environmental risk in transboundary river systems. Rather than estimating measured macroplastic or microplastic concentrations, the proposed approach integrates structural indicators of anthropogenic pressure, environmental vulnerability, and mitigation capacity to support the prioritization of monitoring needs and coordinated circular-economy and river-basin policy interventions.

title: A SAR-derived indicator framework for flood extent, severity, and land-cover vulnerability in a wetland floodplain
abstract: Wetland floodplains require reliable indicators that support flood monitoring and impact assessment under increasing climatic variability. Although satellite remote sensing has improved flood detection, many studies remain focused on binary mapping products, limiting their usefulness for assessing flood magnitude, severity, and land-cover-specific vulnerability. This study develops a satellite-derived indicator framework using multi-temporal Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar and Sentinel-2 optical imagery within a Google Earth Engine environment. A site-specific dry-season land use/land cover (LULC) baseline is derived from Sentinel-2 imagery at 10 m resolution using a Random Forest classifier, achieving 91.10% overall accuracy (κ = 0.880), and serves as a reference condition that reduces misclassification of seasonally inundated agricultural areas. Flood extent is represented as a binary indicator of temporary inundation, obtained by applying change-detection threshold to VV- and VH- polarized SAR backscatter that isolates transient flood signals from permanent water bodies and other stable low-backscatter surfaces. Flood severity is further quantified as an ordinal indicator based on the magnitude of backscatter reduction, distinguishing mild, moderate, and severe inundation. Land-cover-specific vulnerability is assessed as the proportion of each land-cover class affected. Application to the May–June 2022 pre-monsoon flash flood in the haor wetlands of northeastern Bangladesh shows that 1963.45 km 2 (60.41%) of the study area was inundated at peak flooding. Vegetation and cropland accounted for the largest flooded area (1508.25 km 2 ), while bare soil, embankments, and roads exhibited the highest proportional inundation (66.81%). Built-up areas experienced moderate relative exposure (47.74%). Severity analysis indicates that moderate-to-severe inundation dominated the event, with severe flooding concentrated in central wetland basins and major river corridors. The proposed indicators provide a transferable and repeatable framework for flood monitoring, comparative assessment, and management support in wetland-dominated floodplain environments.

title: Identifying bark beetle damage predictors in Austria using interpretable machine learning: Thresholds and management implications
abstract: The increasingly severe and frequent forest damage caused by the European spruce bark beetle ( Ips typographus ) has been systematically surveyed across Europe since the early 2000s, yet underlying drivers remain not fully understood. This study aims to identify key predictors and capture spatiotemporal dynamics of bark beetle damage by analysing annual damage time series from 70 Austrian forest districts (2005–2025) using extreme gradient boosting. We quantified the importance of 18 predictors reflecting preceding forest damage, climate, forest composition and topography. The model was evaluated at the national level and for eight regional clusters. Across Austria, it explained 62% of the variance (R 2 ) in cross-validation and identified 64% of true bark beetle outbreaks. Performance was highest in damage hotspots and lower in less affected regions. Preceding bark beetle damage, outbreaks in neighbouring districts and summer climatic water balance were among the strongest predictors. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values revealed clear thresholds at which damage increased: negative summer climatic water balance (< 0 mm), warm spring temperatures (≥ 14.5 °C), and elevated preceding damage by abiotic events (≥ 2 m 3 ha −1 ) and I. typographus (≥ 1 m 3 ha −1 ). Exceeding these thresholds likely amplifies bark beetle damage in previously less affected regions. We conclude that machine learning-based modelling effectively captures the spatiotemporal dynamics and underlying drivers of bark beetle damage at forest district level. Our findings can advance threshold-based risk assessment systems from national to European levels, supporting bark beetle management and the preservation of ecosystem services under a changing climate.

title: Spatial responses of ecosystem services to future climate change across China in the mid-21st century
abstract: Accurately identifying ecosystem-service (ES) responses to future climate change is essential for improving ecological conservation and restoration and for developing targeted adaptation strategies. However, coherent future response zones across multiple regulating services and their associated predictor patterns remain insufficiently understood. In the current study, we established a comprehensive framework based on Shared Socioeconomic Pathway-Representative Concentration Pathway (SSP-RCP) climate scenarios, by using the Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST) model assessments, hotspot analyses, as well as random forest-Shapley additive explanations (RF-SHAP) interpretable machine learning. We assessed water yield, soil conservation, nitrogen retention, and phosphorus retention responses under future SSP-RCP scenarios across China during 2050–2060 relative to a 2000–2020 baseline. Our results revealed pronounced spatial heterogeneity in China's future ESs. At the provincial scale, the unweighted mean values of water yield and soil conservation increased by 18.1–19.5% and 22.0–25.9%, whereas nitrogen and phosphorus retention decreased by 14.9–18.3% and 11.0–15.7%. Northwestern China formed a consistent positive-response zone for water yield and soil conservation. Conversely, central-eastern China formed a contiguous zone of declining phosphorus retention, while Southern China exhibited minimal response. Strong synergistic coupling was observed among the four ESs, with water-related services displaying highly consistent spatial correlations. RF-SHAP analysis indicated relatively large contributions of climate-change and hydroclimatic predictors within the selected predictor framework for most ES responses. In contrast, nitrogen retention showed broader associations with climatic, topographic, and human-activity conditions. These findings provide a scientific basis for spatially differentiated ecological conservation and climate-resilient governance.

title: Non-linear interactive thresholds of water use efficiency dictate precision ecological zoning across climatic gradients
abstract: Ecosystem water use efficiency (WUE ), the core metric of terrestrial carbon-water coupling, is increasingly studied, yet three gaps persist: nonlinear thresholds have been quantified mainly for single drivers, while thresholds of multi-driver interactions remain largely unquantified; basin-scale assessments rarely disaggregate broad climatic gradients, masking region-specific driver regimes; and identified thresholds are seldom translated into spatially explicit management zones. These gaps motivate a climate-stratified, interaction-aware assessment of WUE thresholds that can inform precision ecological zoning in water-limited basins. Taking the Yellow River Basin ( YRB ), a water-limited basin spanning arid to semi-humid climates, we quantified WUE dynamics from 2001 to 2020 and deciphered its drivers by integrating trend persistence analysis (Theil-Sen, Mann-Kendall, Hurst exponent, coefficient of variation) with an interpretable machine learning framework ( CatBoost / XGBoost-SHAP ). WUE exhibited three climate-mediated regimes: high-efficiency growth with moderate stability in the humid southeast, high fluctuation with low stability in the semi-arid center, and low-level, high-stability in the arid northwest. Dominant drivers reorganized systematically along this gradient, from vegetation-atmosphere interactions, through energy-vegetation co-limitation, to physical environment-moisture control under spatially heterogeneous nonlinear thresholds (e.g., PRES = 59.8 kPa in the Plateau Climate Zone; SWVL = 0.08 m 3 ·m −3 in the Middle Temperate Zone). By nesting four management zones within three climatic strata, the three-tier framework converts climate-regime-specific interaction thresholds into actionable, risk-based zoning; over half of the basin (55.6%) falls into early-warning zones. Coupling multi-driver interaction thresholds with climatic stratification, this framework supports a shift from uniform basin-wide policies to proactive, threshold-driven ecological management and is transferable to other water-limited regions.

title: Killing two birds with one stone: Exploring the dual impacts of National Urban agglomeration policy on carbon emissions and economic resilience in China
abstract: Urban agglomeration policies may reshape both carbon emissions and economic resilience, yet existing studies have largely examined these outcomes separately and at the city level, leaving their joint county-level effects insufficiently understood. This study treats China's national urban agglomeration policy as a quasi-natural experiment and evaluates its effects using panel data for 2129 counties from 2006 to 2023. A staggered difference-in-differences design is supplemented with heterogeneity-robust DID estimators, while mechanism tests and spatial Durbin models are used to examine possible channels and spatial spillovers. The results show that the policy lowers carbon emissions and strengthens economic resilience. These two improvements are particularly evident in eastern counties, those with medium-sized populations, and those with lower spatial concentration. Green innovation capacity and AI industry development emerge as potential channels. The spatial estimates further indicate that the policy is associated with lower carbon emissions and stronger economic resilience in geographically proximate or economically similar counties. These findings highlight the need for differentiated urban agglomeration governance that accounts for both local gains and cross-county spillovers, providing relevant evidence for developing and transition economies pursuing regional integration and low-carbon development.

title: Global forest aboveground biomass dynamics and disturbance attribution (2000–2019): A coordinated statistical framework for sustainable forest management
abstract: Reliable forest aboveground biomass (AGB) estimates are foundational for assessing the global carbon cycle, yet existing satellite products suffer from temporal gaps and spatial inconsistencies. Here, we coordinated three global AGB products (Liu, Xu, and Wigneron) covering 2000–2019 by combining random forest regression with pixel-level bias correction based on vegetation optical depth (VOD) observations. Spatiotemporal trends, structural break-points, and causal drivers were quantified using Theil-Sen slope estimation, Mann-Kendall tests, Pettitt change-point detection, and spatial overlay with Hansen global Forest change and MODIS fire datasets. Independent validation against 2019 spaceborne LiDAR (GEDI L4B) confirmed high consistency for the coordinated product ( R 2 = 0.71, RMSE = 14.96 Mg C ha −1 ), while ground VOD network validation yielded R > 0.7 across over 50% of monitoring sites. Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation revealed that parameter perturbation contributed ∼62% of overall uncertainty without time-dependent error accumulation. Global forest AGB exhibited a statistically significant net increase (slope range: +0.25 to +0.57 Pg C yr −1 , p < 0.01), with 56.89% of forested pixels exhibiting a significant upward trend ( p < 0.05). Pettitt tests identified a climate-driven structural break during 2009–2012 ( p < 0.05), coinciding with a strong El Niño–La Niña transition. Process-based attribution revealed a “growth-dominated gain, degradation-dominated loss” carbon dynamic: Forest growth drove 90%–92% (+0.51 to +2.64 Pg C yr −1 ) of global biomass gain, whereas persistent forest degradation accounted for 89% (−0.43 to −2.25 Pg C yr −1 ) of total loss—Substantially exceeding clear-cut deforestation. These findings highlight the necessity of incorporating degradation-centered monitoring into REDD+ policies and sustainable forest management

title: Integrating ecological supply–demand assessment and interpretable machine learning to reveal nonlinear mechanisms in the Central Yunnan Urban Agglomeration
abstract: Rapid urbanization and climate change have intensified conflicts between ecological supply and human demand, posing substantial challenges to sustainable development in urban agglomerations. This study focuses on the Central Yunnan Urban Agglomeration, China, and develops an integrated framework to characterize ecological supply–demand dynamics and nonlinear driving mechanisms during 2000–2024. Ecological supply was quantified by integrating ecological carrying capacity (ECC) and ecosystem services (ESS) into an ecological supply index (ESI), while ecological demand was assessed using a hazard–exposure–vulnerability framework to construct an ecological demand index (EDI). The ecological supply–demand balance (ESD) was calculated as the difference between ESI and EDI. Self-organizing maps (SOM) were used to classify ecological supply–demand regimes, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) combined with Accumulated Local Effects (ALE) was used to identify nonlinear drivers and threshold effects. The results showed that ecological deficits dominated the study region, with a clear spatial mismatch between high-demand urban areas and high-supply mountainous regions. Four ecological supply–demand regimes were identified, revealing substantial spatial heterogeneity and temporal transitions. Road density, precipitation, elevation, and slope were the dominant drivers, and ALE analysis revealed nonlinear responses and critical ecological thresholds. Compared with conventional linear approaches, the proposed LightGBM–ALE framework improves the interpretation of complex ecological interactions and supports more robust ecological indicator development. This study provides a transferable framework for ecological assessment and spatially differentiated management in mountainous urban agglomerations.

title: The widening biophysical divide in urban systems: Evidence from a 24-year study in Europe
abstract: As most cities in Europe face increasing population concentration, rapid urbanization oftentimes poses a threat to the environment. Due to constantly changing human-environment dynamics, studying the biophysical properties of urban areas becomes a complex task. We studied 690 Functional Urban Areas (FUAs) in Europe and analyzed four biophysical indicators: Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), Leaf Area Index (LAI), Land Surface Temperature (LST), and Evapotranspiration (ET) in Urban Cores (UCs) and Commuting Zones (CZs). CZ-UC differences were also assessed utilizing monthly satellite images over 24 years. Our findings suggest that in the majority of FUAs EVI and LAI are increasing in both CZs and UCs, but the increase rates are faster in CZs, leading to a growing difference. UCs showed a tendency to experience faster LST rise compared to CZs, pointing to the urban heat island effect, particularly in the Mediterranean region, whereas the Mid-Europe/Alps region diverged from this pattern. ET revealed little year-over-year changes, with scarce instances of increases found in Turkey. Random Forest models followed by Shapley analysis revealed that urban and forest land cover fractions had the largest impact on explaining CZ-UC differences. Our results indicate that as urban land expands, it hinders vegetation expansion and increases LST. However, rising temperatures can be potentially mitigated by the increase of forest areas. Furthermore, increases in air temperatures and water surfaces were shown to drive faster increases of ET in CZs relative to UCs. This study provides a comprehensive view of environmental trends in European urban areas, and can act as a guide for finer scale research in the future.

title: Projecting ecological niche trajectories of the endangered large flying-fox (Pteropus vampyrus) under future climate change: Environmental interactions and spatial uncertainty for transboundary conservation
abstract: Climate change and anthropogenic pressures unpredictably alter ecological niches, exacerbating the extinction risk for threatened species. However, spatial projections often suffer from limited transferability and inadequate uncertainty quantification, hindering their application in dynamic conservation planning. Here, utilizing nine bioclimatic, topographic, and land cover variables, we developed an ensemble modeling framework integrating ten machine learning algorithms (AUC: 0.9099 ± 0.0130, TSS: 0.6432 ± 0.0428, and BI: 0.9370 ± 0.0352) to evaluate habitat suitability and climate-driven range shifts for the endangered large flying-fox ( Pteropus vampyrus ), a keystone umbrella species in Southeast Asia. Model interpretability revealed that slope aspect is strongly associated with predicted suitability, reflecting its role in shaping microclimatic exposure, moisture dynamics, and wind shelter, whereas temperature seasonality and precipitation of the driest month support population persistence across fragmented landscapes. Projecting spatial trajectories and mapping explicit uncertainties across three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1–2.6, SSP3–7.0, and SSP5–8.5) spanning three future time horizons (2011–2040, 2041–2070, and 2071–2100) indicated severe contraction and fragmentation of suitable ecological niches, with the area classified as General Decrease (29.13%) being more than threefold larger than the area classified as General Increase (9.29%) under the highest emission scenario SSP5–8.5. Beyond emphasizing the critical necessity of uncertainty quantification in transferability across climate scenarios and rendering ecological interactions transparent through model interpretability techniques, monitoring the current status and changes of the Pteropus vampyrus ecological niche provides valuable scientific evidence, serving as a critical foundation for formulating robust conservation strategies.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and driving mechanisms of plastic pollutant emissions from agricultural greenhouses in China
abstract: Greenhouses are increasingly recognized as hotspots of agricultural plastic pollution, yet the spatiotemporal dynamics of their pollutant emissions and the mechanisms by which natural, management, and socio-economic drivers jointly regulate these emissions remain poorly quantified. Thus, we integrated time-series Landsat imagery on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform with a prefecture-city-level emission inventory to quantify emissions of 2 representative phthalate esters (Dibutyl phthalate (DBP) and Bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP)) from China's agricultural greenhouses during 2005–2024. We then coupled Random Forest (RF) with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpretation to identify dominant drivers and their key thresholds, and applied partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to decompose the direct, indirect, and total effects of latent drivers (natural conditions, on-site management, agricultural development, and urbanization) on emissions. National emissions increased 2.7-fold over the study period (DEHP: from 24.29 t to 65.50 t; DBP: from 12.37 t to 33.35 t) and were strongly spatially concentrated with East China. Driver importance shifted markedly over time, with slope and rural population gaining prominence. Crucially, PLS-SEM revealed pervasive offsetting pathways: for urbanization in 2015, its direct suppressive effect on emissions (−0.195) was more than cancelled by a positive indirect effect operating through agricultural expansion (0.248), yielding a near-zero net effect (−0.015). Thus, a driver's apparent unimportance can mask large but opposing direct and indirect pathways. We conclude that greenhouse expansion simultaneously secures production and amplifies plastic pollutant emissions through a coupled driver network in which indirect mediation dominates. Because an apparently weak driver may merely be internally offset, interventions targeting a single driver are liable to be neutralized; effective control must instead act on the mediating pathways (e.g., agricultural expansion) and be differentiated by region.

title: Assessing and Predicting Ecological Quality Using a Novel Indicator and Machine Learning Framework: A Case Study of Beijing
abstract: Ecological quality is a comprehensive concept that reflects the overall condition of an ecosystem. Understanding its dynamic evolution and future trajectories is essential for sustainable ecosystem management. However, existing studies often rely on single-dimensional perspectives and overlook ecosystem complexity, nonlinear relationships, and interactions among drivers. Therefore, this study developed a novel ecological quality indicator based on a “function–status–disturbance” framework integrating ecosystem services, the Remote Sensing Ecological Index, the Modified Water Area Remote Sensing Ecological Index, and nighttime light intensity. We quantified the spatiotemporal evolution of ecological quality in Beijing from 2000 to 2020. Correlation analysis was used to select ten significant environmental and socioeconomic drivers from eleven candidate variables. A Random Forest model incorporating the ten drivers predicted ecological quality under three representative SSP–RCP scenarios for 2035. Permutation importance based on the percentage increase in mean squared error and partial dependence analysis were used to quantify the relative importance, nonlinear responses, and threshold effects of drivers. The results showed that (1) ecological quality in Beijing exhibited a three-tier concentric gradient pattern, increasing from the urban center to the northwestern mountains. (2) Ecological quality declined overall from 2000 to 2020, particularly during the first decade. (3) The Random Forest model showed high predictive accuracy, with an R 2 of 0.979, an MAE of 0.029 and an RMSE of 0.041. Among the three scenarios in 2035, the ecological protection scenario exhibited the highest ecological quality, followed by the middle path and baseline scenarios, but all remained below the 2020 level. (4) Ecosystem responses varied substantially across scenarios. Natural ecosystems performed best under the ecological protection scenario, whereas cultivated land showed the opposite pattern, with the baseline scenario achieving the highest quality. (5) Annual precipitation and distance to regional centers were the most influential drivers, and most factors exhibited nonlinear and threshold effects. These findings provide scientific support for adaptive ecosystem management and sustainable urban planning.

title: Ecological quality–risk integration reveals spatial management priorities in rapidly urbanizing high-biomass regions
abstract: Rapid urbanization in high-biomass regions has intensified conflicts between ecological conservation and urban expansion, yet conventional assessments may overlook areas where high ecological quality coexists with elevated landscape structural risk. However, the long-term spatial mismatches between ecological quality and landscape ecological risk, together with their nonlinear associations with natural and anthropogenic factors, remain insufficiently understood in rapidly urbanizing high-biomass regions. To address these gaps, this study integrated an improved Remote Sensing Ecological Index (IRSEI) with a Landscape Ecological Risk (LER) model to evaluate ecological quality–risk relationships across Guangdong Province, China. To improve ecological assessment in densely vegetated areas, IRSEI replaced NDVI with the kernel normalized difference vegetation index (kNDVI) and incorporated the abundance index (AI) and net primary productivity (NPP) to represent habitat-support conditions and ecosystem productivity. Standardized IRSEI and LER values were combined through quadrant partitioning, and extreme gradient boosting coupled with SHapley Additive exPlanations (XGBoost–SHAP) was used to examine nonlinear relationships with natural and anthropogenic factors. From 2001 to 2022, ecological quality remained generally stable with a slight upward trend, whereas landscape ecological risk showed substantial spatial changes. The integrated assessment revealed persistent quality–risk mismatches, particularly in areas with relatively high values of both indicators. These Priority Regulation Zones expanded from 6.36% to 8.14% of the study area, suggesting that landscapes with relatively high ecological quality but structural vulnerability may be underestimated by quality-based assessments alone. SHAP results indicated that topographic factors had the strongest associations with both ecological quality and landscape ecological risk, while anthropogenic factors showed nonlinear and stage-dependent relationships. The IRSEI–LER framework thus provides a practical basis for differentiated ecological management in rapidly urbanizing subtropical high-biomass regions.

title: Attribution of changes in vegetation structure and carbon–water fluxes in the Ji-shaped bend of the Yellow River based on process-guided machine learning
abstract: Arid and semi-arid ecosystems play an important role in the global terrestrial carbon cycle, but the relative contributions of climate change, elevated CO₂, and land-use change (LUCC) to their carbon–water processes remain uncertain. In this study, we developed a process-guided machine learning (PGML) framework integrating Biome-BGC and LightGBM, which achieves synergistic simulation of mechanistic constraints and data-driven modeling through residual learning. PGML significantly improved the pixel-scale simulation accuracy of LAI, GPP, and ET in the Ji-shaped Bend of the Yellow River, a typical arid and semi-arid region of China, with R 2 values of 0.70, 0.95, and 0.91, respectively, and reduced RMSE by 61%–83% compared with the calibrated process model. Full-factorial attribution showed that LAI, GPP, ET, and WUE all increased significantly during the study period, with the growth rate of GPP exceeding that of ET, thereby promoting an increase in WUE. Under the process representations and driving factors considered in the PGML framework, elevated CO₂ was identified as the largest simulated contributor to the increases in LAI, GPP, and ET, with contribution rates of 71.8%, 78.7%, and 75.2%, respectively; climate change contributed approximately 15%, while the direct contribution of LUCC was less than 0.25%. Meanwhile, the regional mean climate–CO₂ interaction effect was negative, indicating that local climatic conditions generally weakened the CO₂ fertilization effect. These results reveal that elevated CO₂ made the largest contribution to the enhancement of vegetation structure and carbon–water fluxes in the Ji-shaped Bend of the Yellow River over the past two decades.

title: Asynchronous recovery of grassland ecosystem health in northern China: A three-dimensional assessment of structure, function, and environmental quality
abstract: Assessing ecosystem health under global change remains a central challenge in dryland ecology, as most existing approaches rely on single indices or aggregated metrics that obscure fundamental differences among ecosystem components. Here, we introduce a three-dimensional framework that explicitly separates grassland ecosystem health (GEH) into structural integrity, functional performance, and environmental quality, allowing us to diagnose not only overall trends but also hidden divergences among ecosystem dimensions. Applying this framework to the arid and semi-arid grasslands of northern China over the period 2000–2023, and combining long-term remote sensing data, ecosystem service modeling, and interpretable machine learning, we uncover a previously underappreciated pattern of ecosystem change. We show that GEH has improved overall, but through strongly asynchronous pathways: structural health and environmental quality increased consistently, whereas functional health exhibited a slight but persistent decline. This result challenges the common assumption that vegetation greening and environmental improvement reflect holistic ecosystem recovery. Instead, our findings demonstrate that ecosystem components respond at different rates and through distinct mechanisms, leading to a decoupling between structure, environment, and function. Precipitation emerged as the dominant driver, interacting nonlinearly with topography, and grazing intensity to regulate ecosystem responses. In particular, climate-driven gains in vegetation structure are partially offset by grazing pressure and soil constraints, which limit the recovery of ecosystem services. By explicitly revealing this multidimensional decoupling, our study advances ecosystem health assessment beyond conventional composite indices and identifies asynchronous recovery as a fundamental feature of dryland ecosystems under global change. Critically, this asynchronous decoupling creates a misleading signal of overall ecosystem stability while substantially lowering long-term grassland resilience against extreme drought and intensified human disturbance, generating hidden ecological vulnerability despite widespread vegetation greening. Our results highlight the need to move from structure-based restoration targets toward function-oriented management strategies. The proposed framework provides a transferable tool for diagnosing ecosystem condition and guiding adaptive management across dryland regions worldwide.

title: Divergent responses of cropland GPP and SIF to compound drought and heatwave across China's climatic zones
abstract: Compound drought and heatwave events (CDHWs) pose severe threats to cropland productivity. Yet, climatic zone-specific responses of cropland gross primary productivity (GPP) and solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) to CDHWs remain unclear. This study utilized the machine learning framework coupled with SHAP analysis to reveal the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of CDHWs in China and quantify their impacts on GPP and SIF across different climatic zones. Results showed that moderate, severe, and extreme CDHWs increased significantly in frequency at rates of 0.263, 0.283, and 0.068 events per decade (p < 0.05), respectively, with corresponding increases in duration of 0.158, 0.159, and 0.147 days per decade from 1981 to 2024. Spatially, severe and extreme CDHWs were concentrated in the arid and semi-arid regions of Northwest China, northern North China, and Southwest China. In terms of cropland productivity responses, heatwave-only events increased GPP by 2.74% relative to normal conditions, while drought-only events reduced GPP by 7.10%. Interestingly, CDHWs induced the largest GPP reduction of 12.77%. SHAP analysis further identified relative humidity (RHum) as the dominant negative contributor to GPP under CDHW conditions. For SIF, it exhibited larger response magnitudes to extreme events, declining by 11.72% under drought-only conditions, rising by 73.83% under heatwave-only conditions, and remaining elevated by 61.10% under CDHWs. This elevation was primarily attributed to downward longwave radiation (LRad). Climatic zone-specific analysis demonstrated that LRad, temperature (Temp), and RHum were the three core factors influencing GPP. Notably, Prec exerted the weakest influence, ranging from 0.111 to 0.161. However, LRad was the dominant factor for SIF across all climatic zones, with minimal regional variability. Additionally, RHum contributed nearly as much as Temp to GPP in the BWk zone and ranked as the third-most-important driver of SIF in this region, highlighting the sensitivity of arid ecosystems to atmospheric moisture. This study elucidates the nonlinear impacts of CDHWs on cropland productivity and their climate zone-dependent mechanisms over China, providing critical scientific support for the development of national climate change adaptation strategies and the construction of climate-resilient agricultural systems.

title: Nonlinear impacts and threshold effects of 2D and 3D morphology on ecological resilience across urban functional zones: A case study of Shanghai, China
abstract: Ecological resilience is a key element for urban sustainable development. Understanding spatial morphology's impact mechanism on ecological resilience can help improve ecological resilience under spatial resource constraints. However, existing research lacks systematic exploration of how 2D and 3D morphology affect ecological resilience across different functional zones of megacities. Based on “Tolerance–Absorption–Restoration” framework, this study built an Ecological Resilience Index (ERI) model and taking Shanghai as a case, used Random Forest model and SHAP algorithm for uncovering nonlinear influence and threshold characteristics of 2D and 3D morphology on ecological resilience across functional zones. Results showed that: (1) ERI model can effectively assess ecological resilience across functional zones using multi-source, high-resolution remote sensing data; (2) Ecological resilience in Shanghai presents a “low center, high periphery” pattern. Public service zones exhibit the highest ecological resilience while commercial zones exhibit the lowest, corresponding to spatial distribution gradients of buildings and greenspaces; (3) 2D building morphological indicators exert dominant influence on ecological resilience, while influences of 3D morphology and 2D greenspace morphology exhibit notable scale dependence and regional sensitivity, respectively. Indicators' influences generally show a hierarchy of coverage > cohesion > shape complexity; (4) Morphological impacts exhibit threshold characteristics across functional zones: Zones with higher development intensity show higher thresholds for negative indicators and lower ones for positive indicators. These findings provide quantitative evidence and planning references for differentiated management and ecological resilience improvement across urban functional zones.

title: Overestimated temperature sensitivity in future net primary productivity projections
abstract: Terrestrial net primary productivity (NPP) is a fundamental indicator of ecosystem functioning and carbon sequestration capacity, playing a crucial role in regulating the strength of the land carbon sink. Earth system models (ESMs) are the primary tools for simulating historical NPP variations and projecting future changes. However, NPP projections by ESMs remain subject to substantial uncertainty and bias due to differences in model structure and parameterization. Here, we develop an observation-constrained transfer learning framework that integrates 21 CMIP6 ESMs with satellite-derived NPP to reduce structural biases and constrain future projections. The results indicate that the framework effectively reduces the mean absolute historical bias between ESM simulations and satellite-derived observations by 75.7%. Raw ESM projections show increases in global NPP of 85.88 ± 41.90 and 121.83 ± 67.09 gC m −2 yr −1 under SSP245 and SSP585, respectively. In contrast, observation-constrained projections reduce these increases to 55.23 ± 9.59 and 89.51 ± 18.46 gC m −2 yr −1 , while narrowing the 5th–95th percentile uncertainty range by 78%–82%. Factorial attribution shows that temperature dominates the projected NPP trend among the climatic drivers considered, while precipitation and interaction effects are comparatively small. Temperature-sensitivity analyses further indicate stronger NPP responses to warming in unconstrained ESMs, particularly in tropical regions, whereas observational constraints moderate these responses and lead to lower future NPP projections. Overall, our results suggest that the stronger temperature sensitivity identified in unconstrained ESMs is associated with larger projected increases in terrestrial NPP.

title: Interpretable machine learning reveals environmental controls on carbon-water flux dynamics in a humid subtropical evergreen forest
abstract: Carbon-water coupling in humid subtropical forests is shaped by monsoon variability, yet coordinated changes in carbon uptake, respiration, and water loss remain unclear. We analyzed daily eddy-covariance and meteorological observations across six growing seasons (2020–2025) at Xin'anjiang, Southeast China, including net ecosystem exchange (NEE), gross primary productivity (GPP), ecosystem respiration (R eco ), evapotranspiration (ET), and water-use efficiency (WUE). To distinguish predictive contributions, nonlinear model responses, and covariate-adjusted associations under correlated predictors, we combined nested leave-one-growing-season-out XGBoost with SHAP, ALE, and EconML and paired gap-filled/non-gap-filled analyses. The forest remained a net carbon sink, but indicators varied asynchronously. During DOY 160–190, clustered rainfall and high humidity coincided with lower radiation; reduced GPP and net carbon uptake, comparatively high ET, and the seasonal WUE minimum. Interannually, NEE reflected the balance between GPP and R eco , whereas WUE depended on relative changes in GPP and total ET. Out-of-year R 2 ranged from 0.66 to 0.82, and the schemes shared 70–90% of their Top-10 predictors. Current atmospheric-energy conditions dominated NEE, GPP, and ET predictions; R eco was associated with temperature and antecedent moisture, whereas WUE retained information from atmospheric pressure and soil moisture. Nonlinear responses were clearest for radiation, temperature, and atmospheric pressure, while pairwise interactions were generally weak and covariate-adjusted associations were consistent across schemes. Together, monsoon-related carbon-water variation reflected immediate atmospheric-energy variability conditioned by slower hydrological memory. Although site-specific quantitative results require multi-site evaluation, this multi-flux framework may inform carbon-water-coupling studies in other monsoon-affected forests.

title: Spatio-temporal monitoring of agricultural drought in China based on downscaled soil moisture data
abstract: Abstract. Agricultural drought threatens China's food and ecological security, and accurate spatio-temporal monitoring is key for disaster mitigation. Soil moisture is critical for drought assessment, but the accuracy of existing remote sensing-based SM products in China remains to be improved. This study develops a framework that synergistically integrates a spatiotemporally adaptive gap-filling algorithm with a machine learning-based downscaling approach, generating a seamless 0.05° monthly SM dataset for China from 2003 to 2023. The methodology harnesses the complementary strengths of random forest modeling and spatiotemporal reconstruction techniques to effectively fuse multi-source satellite observations, achieving dual improvements in SM data accuracy and spatial coverage. Using this dataset, the standardized soil moisture index was applied to characterize the spatio-temporal evolution of agricultural drought. Results demonstrate that (1) The downscaled SM dataset achieves significant improvements in both spatial resolution and accuracy, showing a 2.3–34.4 % reduction in ubRMSE and 1.2–52.7 % improvement in correlation coefficients compared to benchmark datasets. (2) Drought characterization based on the downscaled SM dataset and SSI accurately identified the extent of agricultural drought, showing a significant spatiotemporal consistency with agricultural disaster area. (3) Agricultural drought intensified significantly across China during the study period, characterized by northward migration of drought center and spatially heterogeneous aridification patterns – decreasing severity from northwest to southeast while increasing from northeast to southwest. High-frequency drought zones were predominantly clustered in ecologically vulnerable regions, particularly the agro-pastoral ecotone of northern China. (4) Distinct intra-annual drought dynamics emerged, with a southwest-to-northeast expansion dominating from January to June, followed by bidirectional propagation from the Yellow River-Huaihe River Basin (YRB-HRB) to northwestern and southeastern regions from June to December. This study provides high-accuracy data support for agricultural drought monitoring and offers scientific insights for developing regional differentiated drought mitigation strategies, which are of great significance for ensuring national food security.

title: What drives the uphill expansion of cultivated land in hilly regions? Nonlinear responses and threshold effects from the Jiangnan hilly region, China
abstract: Amid the severe challenges to global food security and sustainable development, changes in cultivated land resources have become a key issue in global development research. However, in the context of rapid urbanization, high-quality cultivated land in hilly regions continues to be lost, forcing agricultural activities onto marginal lands. This has led to the phenomenon of uphill expansion of cultivated land, which affects both agricultural sustainability and ecological security. This research characterizes the spatiotemporal evolution of cultivated land expansion in the Jiangnan hilly region of China, revealing a shift from low-gradient areas to increasing encroachment into medium- and high-gradient regions. The results show that while cultivated land continues to expand into higher slopes, the process slows significantly beyond a 10° slope due to topographic limitations. To explore the underlying driving mechanisms, a Geographically Weighted Random Forest model is employed to examine the spatial heterogeneity of these driving factors. The findings indicate that net income per farmer is the primary driver, reflecting the dominant role of farmers' economic decisions. Additionally, built-up land expansion area exerts a spatial compression effect, driving cultivated land into steeper areas. Ultimately, the uphill expansion of cultivated land is a nonlinear response to socio-economic pressures exceeding the region's ecological carrying capacity. This study provides policy implications for hilly regions, suggesting the integration of slope-based ecological constraints within the “land occupation–compensation balance” framework to promote sustainable land use.

title: Identifying land use thresholds for ecosystem service balance through supply-demand assessment in Hainan Island
abstract: Against the backdrop of accelerating urbanization, the imbalance between ecosystem services (ESs) supply and demand has become a major concern for regional sustainable development, particularly in geographically isolated islands, where spatially confined land resources limit the self-regulatory capacity of terrestrial ESs and amplify their vulnerability to supply-demand imbalance. Using Hainan Island as a case study, we integrated the InVEST model, random forest algorithm, and weighted linear regression to quantify the spatiotemporal supply-demand dynamics of five core ESs from 2010 to 2020, identified key land-use thresholds governing ESs balance, and established a dual-scale analytical framework at county and grid levels. The results revealed a pronounced spatial dichotomy of “coastal degradation versus central stability”. Central forests sustained surpluses in regulating services (Habitat Quality (HQ), Soil Retention (SR) and Carbon Sequestration (CS)), while deficit zones clustered in coastal towns. Contribution analysis of land-use types to the ecological supply-demand ratio (ESDR) identified built-up land as the primary negative driver of imbalance. Built-up expansion contributed to supply-demand deficits in Water Retention (WR), with mean ESDR values of − 0.0090 in 2020 and induced imbalance risks for Grain Production (GP) in half of the counties at the county scale. At the 500 m grid scale, 87.71% of the island maintained simultaneous supply-demand balance across all five services. Threshold analysis identified a structural land-use dilemma: attempting to achieve GP balance through forest-to-cropland conversion triggers a “denominator effect”, mechanically increasing built-up land proportions and pushing locally bound regulating services beyond their critical thresholds. This reflects an asymmetry in compensability, as GP deficits can be mitigated via external trade networks whereas regulating services are difficult to compensate externally. At the county scale, five management zones (“maintained zone”, “GP promoted zone”, “CS promoted zone”, “GP-CS promoted zone”, and “GP-CS-WR promoted zone”) were delineated to safeguard ecological cores and address spatially differentiated deficits; at the grid scale, 87.71% of the study area currently maintains ESs balance across all five services, with the identified land-use thresholds serving as early-warning indicators to guide timely regulation of built-up expansion. The integrated analytical framework established in this study is potentially transferable to other tropical islands facing land resource constraints, while the empirical threshold values necessitate site-specific calibration for regional adaptation. This threshold-based governance paradigm offers a practical and quantitative reference for alleviating structural trade-offs in ESs and optimizing ecological management strategies for land constrained island regions.

title: Impact of hydropower construction on vegetation NPP in the Yarlung Zangbo River, Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
abstract: Vegetation net primary production (NPP) is integral to the global carbon cycle, especially in the alpine ecosystems of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. However, hydropower construction can profoundly disrupt ecosystem health and carbon sequestration capacity, particularly along the Yarlung Zangbo River. Therefore, there is an urgent need to understand the impacts of hydropower construction on riparian vegetation NPP through precise, engineering-scale assessments of long-term changes. Changes in NPP may alter soil carbon inputs and turnover, with potential feedbacks on ecosystem carbon balance. Such assessments are essential for comprehensive ecological evaluations of hydropower projects. In this study, we downscaled MODIS NPP data to 30 m resolution using a convolutional neural network-based model to examine the spatiotemporal dynamics of NPP changes at the engineering scale across disturbance zones (DZs) and influence zones (IZs). We further applied a structural equation model (SEM) and a generalized linear model (GLM) to enable process-based attribution of dam- and climate-driven changes in NPP from the pre-construction, during-construction, to post-construction stages. The results showed that hydropower construction caused persistent NPP reductions in DZs due to engineered surface expansion and vegetation loss, whereas IZs experienced a sharp NPP decline during construction (88.6%), followed by widespread recovery in the post-construction stage (93.9%). The SEM–GLM framework identified dam construction as the predominant driver of NPP variations (standardized path coefficient: −0.35 in DZs; mean relative importance: 38.6% in IZs), exceeding the combined effects of precipitation and temperature. These findings provide critical insights for ecological risk assessment, sustainable ecosystem management, and the coordinated development of engineering infrastructure and the natural environment in future hydropower projects in environmentally sensitive alpine regions.

title: Hydrological-state reorganization of eutrophication risk in temperate monsoon coastal rivers revealed by interpretable machine learning and structural path analysis
abstract: Hydrological-state variability strongly shapes eutrophication risk in small coastal catchments, but the transition from low-flow source accumulation to rainfall-driven transport remains poorly quantified. We analysed monthly eutrophication index (EI) patterns for 30 coastal rivers on the Shandong Peninsula, China, from 2020 to 2024 using an integrated interpretable machine-learning and observed-variable structural path-analysis framework. The EI, derived from TN, TP, DO, and COD Mn , was evaluated against terrain, hydroclimate, hydrology, human activity, point-source pollution, and anthropogenic-pressure proxies derived from annual wastewater and fertilizer inventories. EI was significantly higher under high-flow conditions than under low- and transition-flow conditions, accompanied by marked changes in the relative contributions of the individual EI components. Predictor associations also varied across hydrological states. Low-flow conditions were more closely associated with river discharge (Q), human pressure, and downstream catchment setting, whereas transition-flow conditions showed a stronger terrain-related association structure. Under high-flow conditions, human-activity, terrain, precipitation, and Q signals were more broadly represented. Structural path analysis further showed that precipitation was positively associated with Q and the TP- and COD Mn -related components under high-flow conditions, whereas temperature- and HFI-related associations were more evident under transition- and low-flow conditions. Overall, the results reveal a hydrological-state-dependent reorganization of eutrophication risk and its environmental associations, providing a basis for flow-state-specific water-quality monitoring.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of ecological quality across frozen-ground zones in Northeast China: A modified RSEI and explainable GeoAI framework
abstract: Reliable ecological quality assessment is essential for early detection of environmental risks in cold regions. However, conventional indices such as the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) often overlook snow cover and ground thermal conditions that shape ecosystem functioning. Using northeast China, a representative mid-latitude permafrost transition zone, as a case study, we developed a modified remote sensing ecological index (MRSEI) incorporating snow cover fraction (SCF) and soil temperature (ST), and established an explainable geospatial artificial intelligence (XGeoAI) framework to quantify the spatially heterogeneous effects of natural and anthropogenic drivers. Results show that: (1) ecological quality in the NCPR exhibited a dual-phase pattern, with degradation during 2005–2015 followed by restoration during 2015–2020; (2) mean MRSEI values across the four frozen-ground zones decreased progressively from 0.662 in the predominantly continuous permafrost zone to 0.313 in the moderately thick seasonally frozen ground zone, representing an overall decline of 0.349 (52.7%), with intermediate values of 0.547 and 0.421 in the predominantly continuous and island permafrost zone and the sparsely island permafrost zone, respectively; and (3) ecological quality variation was governed by nonlinear, spatially heterogeneous, and interactive effects, with natural background conditions playing stronger roles in northern and mountainous permafrost areas, whereas human disturbance factors exerted stronger negative effects in the central–southern regions and the moderately thick seasonally frozen ground zone. These findings demonstrate the suitability of MRSEI for cryospheric ecological monitoring and the value of XGeoAI for supporting spatially targeted ecological management.

title: Identifying spatiotemporal patterns and associated determinants of stable natural vegetation resilience across China
abstract: Vegetation resilience (VR) is a critical factor in ecosystem stability. Previous studies in China have mainly focused on vegetation restoration monitoring rather than resilience dynamic identification and their heterogeneous drivers, which may be insufficient for ensuring ecosystem restoration efficacy as well as afforestation management and optimization. Therefore, the present work quantified VR as the negative first-order autoregressive coefficient (−AR(1)) of detrended and deseasonalized vegetation anomalies obtained from MODIS kNDVI (kernel normalized difference vegetation index) from 2000 to 2025. We combined 60-month sliding windows with interpretable machine learning, ecosystem-specific models, and geographically weighted regression to examine spatial patterns, temporal trajectories, and environmental determinants of VR. VR was generally higher in southern and eastern China, with relatively low values in parts of the Inner Mongolian and Loess Plateau. Grassland resilience declined substantially with latitude, whereas the corresponding relationship for forests was weak. Although most of the vegetated areas lacked monotonic trends, nonlinear trajectories were widespread. The dominant increase-then-decrease mode of VR change accounted for approximately one-third of the classified area, indicating that earlier improvements of VR were often unsustainable. Climatic variables accounted for 61.8% of the total model importance for VR, with mean soil moisture contributing to approximately one-third. Soil moisture, vapor pressure deficit, and topography showed threshold-dependent or non-monotonic associations with VR. Grasslands were more sensitive to vapor pressure deficit variability, soil moisture, and soil organic carbon than forests, and the local regression coefficient revealed strong spatial nonstationarity. These findings reveal the complex climatic drivers of VR and provide a scientific basis upon which ecosystem restoration efforts can be optimized across China and beyond.

title: Impacts of climate change on the distribution of waterbird ecological corridors in Northeast China and implications for the Post-2020 global biodiversity framework
abstract: Global warming has substantially altered the distribution of waterbird ecological corridors. However, the mechanisms driving these changes remain poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, we developed a coupled climate–habitat–ecological corridor analytical framework integrating the least-cost path model, circuit theory, the Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model, and the eXtreme Gradient Boosting–SHapley Additive exPlanations interpretation approach. Using Northeast China as the study area, the framework was applied to simulate and predict the distribution of least-cost corridors, ecological nodes, and habitat suitability for three waterbird species ( Grus japonensis , Cygnus cygnus , and Mergus squamatus ) during the historical period and three future time periods (the 2030s, 2050s, and 2070s). The framework was further used to quantify the relative contributions of environmental drivers to the distribution of waterbird ecological corridors. The results indicate that: (1) under climatic filtering, non-narrow-range species with broader niche breadth generally maintained relatively stable corridor number and length, whereas narrow-range species exhibited greater temporal variability in corridor patterns, particularly in habitat area and corridor number density; and (2) at the regional scale, climatic factors are strongly associated with the distribution of waterbird ecological corridors, likely through their effects on physiological suitability and resource availability. Elevation and local habitat attributes provide additional environmental constraints that drive these climate–corridor associations. By examining the associations among climate, elevation, habitat, and ecological corridor distribution within a coupled-system framework, this study highlights the urgent need to integrate climatic considerations into corridor conservation planning in support of the Post-2020 Global Biodiversity Framework.

title: Global patterns and projected shifts in factors influencing staple crop yield stability
abstract: Climate change is increasingly destabilizing global agricultural systems by amplifying climate variability and intensifying extreme weather and climate events, yet the factors associated with variation in crop yield stability remain insufficiently quantified. Using global crop-yield data at a 0.5° spatial resolution, we developed a multilevel framework integrating random forest modeling and SHAP-based interpretation of predictor contributions at the variable, factor-category, and contribution-direction levels. We quantified associations of climate, management, and soil factors with yield stability in winter wheat, spring wheat, soybean, and maize, and assessed potential shifts in the leading predictors under three future climate scenarios. Historical yield stability exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity. Areas with low stability (yield stability <4) accounted for 13.3%, 30.1%, 0.86%, and 8.03% of the cultivated areas of winter wheat, spring wheat, soybean, and maize, respectively, and were concentrated mainly in low- to mid-latitudes and hot, dry transition zones. Mean climate was the leading factor category associated with historical stability in winter wheat, spring wheat, and soybean, whereas climate variability contributed more prominently for maize. Under future scenarios, global mean yield stability during 2031–2100 was projected to decline by 6–33%, 11–34%, and 13–41% under SSP1–RCP2.6, SSP2–RCP4.5, and SSP5–RCP8.5, respectively. The area fraction in which climate variability or extremes made the largest SHAP contribution increased by more than 30% relative to the historical period, with the greatest expansion under SSP5–RCP8.5. Although management–soil contributions partially offset negative climate contributions in some regions, the projections suggest that maintaining historical conditions may be insufficient to counter future climatic risks. Overall, our results reveal a systematic shift in the leading correlates of yield stability from mean climate toward climate variability and extremes, highlighting escalating risks to global food security.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and influencing factors of urban flood resilience in urban agglomerations using explainable machine learning: a case study of the middle reaches of the Yangtze River urban agglomeration
abstract: Climate change and rapid urbanization are intensifying urban flood risks. Improving urban flood resilience (UFR) requires identifying key influencing factors, their effective ranges, interactions, and critical thresholds. This study examines the Middle Reaches of the Yangtze River Urban Agglomeration using multi-source data from 2012 to 2023. A Driving forces–Pressure–State–Impact–Response (DPSIR) framework was developed to assess UFR. Spatial statistics and the Space-Time Cube were used to reveal its spatiotemporal evolution. XGBoost, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and partial dependence plots (PDPs) were applied to identify nonlinear thresholds and interactions among influencing factors. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was further used to examine structural associations between influencing factors and DPSIR dimensions and among the dimensions themselves. Results show an overall improvement in UFR, with Wuhan, Changsha, and Nanchang forming major high-resilience cores. Low-value lock-in persisted around Wuhan, whereas Changsha and Nanchang exhibited outward-spreading spatial patterns. Technology level (Tech) and fiscal self-sufficiency rate (FSR) remained the most important factors, while most key associations showed clear nonlinear and threshold characteristics. Tech–FSR interactions were consistently the strongest, but the interaction structure gradually expanded to include natural factors such as elevation (DEM) and slope (SLO). SEM results revealed generally stable but stage-dependent structural associations, with natural geographic factors becoming more strongly associated with the State dimension in later years. These findings clarify the spatiotemporal evolution, nonlinear influences, and structural relationships of UFR, providing evidence for cross-regional flood governance and targeted resource allocation in urban agglomerations.
